sentences.zh: 尹昌隆，字彥謙，泰和人。

translations.literal: Yin Changlong, styled Yanqian, was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Changlong, styled Yanqian, was a native of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 洪武中進士及第。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era he passed the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign he passed the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 授修撰，改監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler, then transferred to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Compiler, then transferred to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 惠帝初即位，視朝晏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui first took the throne, he held court at a late hour.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui first took the throne, he held court at a late hour.

sentences.zh: 昌隆疏諫曰：「高皇帝雞鳴而起，昧爽而朝，未日出而臨百官，故能庶績咸熙，天下乂安。

translations.literal: Changlong submitted a memorial remonstrating: "The Grand Emperor rose at cockcrow, held court at dawn, and received the myriad officials before the sun had risen; thus all affairs flourished and the realm was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Changlong submitted a memorial remonstrating: "The Grand Emperor rose at cockcrow, held court at dawn, and received the myriad officials before the sun had risen; thus all affairs flourished and the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣守大業，宜追繩祖武，兢兢業業，憂勤萬幾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has inherited and preserved the great enterprise; you ought to follow your ancestor's example, be diligent and careful, and labor anxiously over the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has inherited and preserved the great enterprise; you ought to follow your ancestor's example, be diligent and careful, and labor anxiously over the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 今乃即於晏安，日上數刻，猶未臨朝。

translations.literal: Yet now you rest in ease, and when the sun has mounted several notches you still have not held court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you rest in ease, and when the sun has mounted several notches you still have not held court.

sentences.zh: 群臣宿衛，疲於伺候，曠職廢業，上下懈弛。

translations.literal: Ministers standing guard day and night grow weary waiting; offices are neglected and work abandoned; above and below lapse into slackness.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers standing guard day and night grow weary waiting; offices are neglected and work abandoned; above and below lapse into slackness.

sentences.zh: 播之天下，傳之四裔，非社稷福也。」

translations.literal: Spread this through the realm and abroad to the four quarters, and it is no blessing to the altars of land and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Spread this through the realm and abroad to the four quarters, and it is no blessing to the altars of land and grain."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昌隆言切直，禮部其宣示天下，使知朕過。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Changlong's words are blunt and direct; let the Ministry of Rites proclaim them throughout the realm so all may know my fault."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Changlong's words are blunt and direct; let the Ministry of Rites proclaim them throughout the realm so all may know my fault."

sentences.zh: 未幾，以地震上言，謫福寧知縣。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of a memorial submitted after an earthquake, he was demoted to magistrate of Funing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on account of a memorial submitted after an earthquake, he was demoted to magistrate of Funing.

sentences.zh: 燕兵既逼，昌隆以北來奏章動引周公輔成王為詞，勸帝罷兵，許王入朝。

translations.literal: When the Yan armies drew near, Changlong's memorials arriving from the north repeatedly cited the Duke of Zhou assisting King Cheng as a precedent, urging the emperor to cease fighting and allow the prince entry to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan armies drew near, Changlong's memorials arriving from the north repeatedly cited the Duke of Zhou assisting King Cheng as a precedent, urging the emperor to cease fighting and allow the prince entry to court.

sentences.zh: 設有蹉跌，便舉位讓之。

translations.literal: If there should be some mishap, you should at once yield the throne to him.
translations.idiomatic: If there should be some mishap, you should at once yield the throne to him.

sentences.zh: 若沈吟不斷，進退失據，將求為丹徒布衣且不可得。

translations.literal: If you hesitate and cannot decide, losing your footing whether to advance or retreat, you will not even be able to seek the status of a common cloth-clad man of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and cannot decide, losing your footing whether to advance or retreat, you will not even be able to seek the status of a common cloth-clad man of Dantu.

sentences.zh: 成祖入京師，昌隆名在奸臣中。

translations.literal: When Chengzu entered the capital, Changlong's name was listed among treacherous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu entered the capital, Changlong's name was listed among treacherous ministers.

sentences.zh: 以前奏貸死，命傅世子於北平。

translations.literal: Because of his earlier memorial his life was spared; he was ordered to attend the heir apparent at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his earlier memorial his life was spared; he was ordered to attend the heir apparent at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年冊世子為皇太子，擢昌隆左春坊左中允。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle the heir apparent was installed as crown prince, and Changlong was promoted to Left Vice-Director in the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 2 the heir apparent was installed as crown prince, and Changlong was promoted to Left Vice-Director in the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 隨事匡諫，太子甚重之。

translations.literal: He admonished the prince on every matter, and the prince valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: He admonished the prince on every matter, and the crown prince valued him greatly.

sentences.zh: 解縉之黜，同日改昌隆禮部主事。

translations.literal: On the day Xie Jin was dismissed, Changlong was transferred the same day to Secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xie Jin was dismissed, Changlong was transferred that same day to Secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尚書呂震方用事，性刻忮。

translations.literal: Minister Lü Zhen was then in power, harsh and jealous by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lü Zhen was then in power, by nature harsh and jealous.

sentences.zh: 當其獨處精思，以手指刮眉尾，則必有密謀深計。

translations.literal: When he sat alone in deep thought and stroked the ends of his brows with his fingers, he was sure to be forming some secret, far-reaching plan.
translations.idiomatic: When he sat alone in deep thought and stroked the ends of his brows with his fingers, he was sure to be hatching some secret, far-reaching scheme.

sentences.zh: 官屬相戒，無敢白事者。

translations.literal: Subordinates warned one another, and none dared report business to him.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates warned one another, and none dared bring business before him.

sentences.zh: 昌隆前白事，震怒不應；

translations.literal: Changlong went forward to report business; Zhen was angry and did not respond;
translations.idiomatic: Changlong went forward to report business; Zhen was angry and did not answer;

sentences.zh: 移時又白之，震愈怒，拂衣起。

translations.literal: after a while he reported again; Zhen grew angrier, rose, and flung off his robe.
translations.idiomatic: After a while he reported again; Zhen grew still angrier, rose, and flung off his robe.

sentences.zh: 昌隆退白太子，取令旨行之。

translations.literal: Changlong withdrew and reported to the crown prince, took an order from him, and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Changlong withdrew and reported to the crown prince, obtained an order from him, and carried it out.

sentences.zh: 震大怒，奏昌隆假托宮僚，陰欲樹結，潛蓄無君心。

translations.literal: Zhen was greatly enraged and memorialized that Changlong had falsely used his post in the palace staff, secretly sought to build a faction, and harbored a heart disloyal to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was greatly enraged and memorialized that Changlong had falsely used his post among the palace staff, secretly sought to build a faction, and harbored disloyal designs against the throne.

sentences.zh: 逮下獄。

translations.literal: He was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 尋遇赦復官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was pardoned and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was pardoned and restored to office.

sentences.zh: 父憂起復。

translations.literal: After mourning for his father he returned to service.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his father he returned to service.

sentences.zh: 謁震，震溫言接之。

translations.literal: He called on Zhen; Zhen received him with mild words.
translations.idiomatic: He called on Zhen; Zhen received him with mild words.

sentences.zh: 入理前奏，復下錦衣衛獄，籍其家。

translations.literal: When he entered the ministry he repeated his earlier memorial; he was again sent to the Brocade Guard prison and his household goods were registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered the ministry he repeated his earlier memorial; he was again sent to the Brocade Guard prison and his household goods were registered and confiscated.

sentences.zh: 帝凡巡幸，下詔獄者率輿以從，謂之隨駕重囚，昌隆與焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour, those in the imperial prison were usually carried in litters to follow him, called "heavy prisoners accompanying the imperial procession"; Changlong was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on tour, those in the imperial prison were usually carried in litters to follow him—called "heavy prisoners accompanying the imperial procession"—and Changlong was among them.

sentences.zh: 後數年，谷王謀反事發。

translations.literal: Several years later the Prince of Gu's plot to rebel came to light.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the Prince of Gu's plot to rebel came to light.

sentences.zh: 以王前奏昌隆為長史，坐以同謀，詔公卿雜問。

translations.literal: Because the prince had earlier memorialized recommending Changlong as chief steward, Changlong was charged as a co-conspirator, and the emperor ordered the dukes and ministers to question him jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Because the prince had earlier memorialized recommending Changlong as chief steward, Changlong was charged as a co-conspirator, and the emperor ordered the dukes and ministers to question him jointly.

sentences.zh: 昌隆辯不已，震折之。

translations.literal: Changlong defended himself without cease; Zhen rebutted him.
translations.idiomatic: Changlong defended himself without cease; Zhen rebutted him.

sentences.zh: 獄具，置極刑死，夷其族。

translations.literal: When the case was complete he was put to the extreme penalty and died; his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete he was put to the extreme penalty and died; his clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 後震病且死，號呼「尹相」，言見昌隆守欲殺之雲。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhen was ill and near death, he cried out "Minister Yin," saying he saw Changlong standing by, wanting to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhen was ill and near death, he cried out "Minister Yin," saying he saw Changlong standing by and wanting to kill him.

sentences.zh: 耿通，齊東人。

translations.literal: Geng Tong was a native of Qidong.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Tong was a native of Qidong.

sentences.zh: 洪武中舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 授襄陽教授。

translations.literal: He was appointed instructor at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed instructor at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，擢刑科給事中，歷左右給事。

translations.literal: In the early Yongle reign he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments, and served through the left and right supervising-secretary posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongle reign he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments, and served through the left and right supervising-secretary posts.

sentences.zh: 剛直敢言。

translations.literal: Upright and bold in speech.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and bold in speech.

sentences.zh: 嘗劾都御史陳瑛、御史袁綱、覃珩朋比為蒙蔽，構陷無辜，綱、珩已下獄，瑛長官，不宜獨宥。

translations.literal: He once impeached Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying and censors Yuan Gang and Tan Heng for banding together to deceive and framing the innocent; Gang and Heng were already in prison, but Ying was the chief official and should not alone be spared.
translations.idiomatic: He once impeached Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying and Censors Yuan Gang and Tan Heng for banding together to deceive the court and framing the innocent; Gang and Heng were already in prison, but Ying was the chief official and ought not to be spared alone.

sentences.zh: 又言：驍騎諸衛倉壞，工部侍郎陳壽不預修，糧至無所受，多損耗病民；

translations.literal: He also said: the storehouses of the vigilant-cavalry guards were in ruins; Vice Minister Chen Shou of the Ministry of Works had not undertaken repairs; grain arrived but there was nowhere to receive it, and much was lost or wasted, harming the people;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: the storehouses of the vigilant-cavalry guards were in ruins; Vice Minister Chen Shou of the Ministry of Works had not undertaken repairs; when grain arrived there was nowhere to receive it, and much was lost or wasted, to the people's harm;

sentences.zh: 工部尚書宋禮不恤下，匠役滿，不即遣歸，多至失所。

translations.literal: Minister Song Li of the Ministry of Works was uncaring toward subordinates; when craftsmen and corvée laborers finished their term he did not send them home at once, and many came to destitution.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Song Li of the Ministry of Works was uncaring toward subordinates; when craftsmen and corvée laborers finished their term he did not send them home at once, and many were left destitute.

sentences.zh: 瑛等皆被鐫責。

translations.literal: Ying and the others were all fined and reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and the others were all fined and reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 當是時，給事中敢言者，通與陳諤。

translations.literal: At that time among supervising secretaries who dared speak out, Tong and Chen E were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: At that time among supervising secretaries who dared speak out, Tong and Chen E stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 舉朝憚其風采。

translations.literal: The whole court stood in awe of their presence.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court stood in awe of their bearing.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢大理寺右丞。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to Vice Director of the Right in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was promoted to Vice Director of the Right in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 帝北巡，太子監國。

translations.literal: The emperor toured the north while the crown prince governed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor toured the north while the crown prince governed the realm.

sentences.zh: 漢王高煦謀奪嫡，陰結帝左右為讒間，宮僚多得罪者。

translations.literal: Prince Han Gao Xu plotted to seize the succession, secretly winning over those close to the emperor to slander and divide, and many of the palace staff suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Han Zhu Gaoxu plotted to seize the succession, secretly winning over those close to the emperor to slander and divide father and son, and many of the palace staff suffered punishment.

sentences.zh: 監國所行事，率多更置。

translations.literal: Affairs decided during the regency were mostly overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs decided during the regency were mostly overturned.

sentences.zh: 通從容諫帝：「太子事無大過誤，可無更也。」

translations.literal: Tong calmly admonished the emperor: "The crown prince's affairs have no great errors; there is no need to change them."
translations.idiomatic: Tong calmly admonished the emperor: "The crown prince's affairs have no great errors; there is no need to change them."

sentences.zh: 數言之，帝不悅。

translations.literal: He spoke thus several times; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke thus several times; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 十年秋，有言通受請托故出人罪者。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year someone said Tong had accepted bribes and therefore released guilty persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the tenth year someone said Tong had accepted bribes and therefore released guilty persons.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，命都察院會文武大臣鞫之午門，曰：「必殺通無赦。」

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and ordered the Censorate together with civil and military ministers to try him at the Meridian Gate, saying: "Tong must be killed without pardon."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered the Censorate together with civil and military ministers to try him at the Meridian Gate, saying: "Tong must be killed without pardon."

sentences.zh: 群臣如旨，當通罪斬。

translations.literal: The ministers obeyed the intent, and fixed Tong's crime as death by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers obeyed the intent and fixed Tong's crime as death by decapitation.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「失出，細故耳，通為東宮關說，壞祖法，離間我父子，不可恕，其置之極刑。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wrongful release is a petty matter; Tong pleaded for the Eastern Palace, violated ancestral law, and drove a wedge between father and son—unforgivable. Put him to the extreme penalty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Wrongful release is a petty matter; Tong pleaded for the Eastern Palace, violated ancestral law, and drove a wedge between father and son—unforgivable. Put him to the extreme penalty."

sentences.zh: 廷臣不敢爭，竟論奸黨，磔死。

translations.literal: Court ministers did not dare dispute; in the end he was judged a treasonous faction member and died by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers did not dare dispute; in the end he was judged a treasonous faction member and died by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 陳諤，字克忠，番愚人。

translations.literal: Chen E, styled Kezhong, was a native of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen E, styled Kezhong, was a native of Panyu.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，以鄉舉入太學，授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era, through the provincial examination he entered the Imperial Academy and was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle era, through the provincial examination he entered the Imperial Academy and was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 遇事剛果，彈劾無所避。

translations.literal: In affairs he was firm and resolute; in impeachment he spared no one.
translations.idiomatic: In affairs he was firm and resolute; in impeachment he spared no one.

sentences.zh: 每奏事，大聲如鐘。

translations.literal: Whenever he presented a memorial his voice was loud as a bell.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he presented a memorial his voice rang out like a bell.

sentences.zh: 帝令餓之數日，奏對如故。

translations.literal: The emperor had him starved for several days; his answers in audience were as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him starved for several days; his answers in audience were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 曰：「是天性也。」

translations.literal: He said: "It is his nature."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "It is his nature."

sentences.zh: 每見，呼為「大聲秀才」。

translations.literal: Whenever he appeared, the emperor called him "the Loud-voiced Graduate."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he appeared, the emperor called him "the Loud-voiced Graduate."

sentences.zh: 嘗言事忤旨，命坎瘞奉天門，露其首。

translations.literal: Once when he spoke on policy contrary to the imperial will, he was ordered buried alive at Fengtian Gate with his head exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he spoke on policy contrary to the imperial will, he was ordered buried alive at Fengtian Gate with his head exposed.

sentences.zh: 七日不死，赦出還職。

translations.literal: After seven days he did not die; he was pardoned and returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: After seven days he did not die; he was pardoned and returned to office.

sentences.zh: 已，復忤旨，罰修象房。

translations.literal: Later he again offended the will and was punished by being ordered to repair the elephant quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again offended the will and was punished by being ordered to repair the elephant quarters.

sentences.zh: 貧不能雇役，躬自操作。

translations.literal: Poor and unable to hire laborers, he worked with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to hire laborers, he worked with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 適駕至，問為誰。

translations.literal: Just then the imperial procession arrived; the emperor asked who he was.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the imperial procession arrived; the emperor asked who he was.

sentences.zh: 諤匍匐前，具道所以。

translations.literal: E crawled forward and explained the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: E crawled forward and explained the whole affair in detail.

sentences.zh: 帝憐之，命復官。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and ordered his office restored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied him and ordered his office restored.

sentences.zh: 歷任順天府尹，政尚嚴鷙。

translations.literal: Having served in succession as Prefect of Shuntian, his administration favored severity and rigor.
translations.idiomatic: Having served in succession as Prefect of Shuntian, he governed with severity and rigor.

sentences.zh: 執政忌之，出為湖廣按察使。

translations.literal: The ruling ministers resented him, and he was sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: The ruling ministers resented him, and he was sent out as Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 改山西，坐事落職。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shanxi, he was dismissed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shanxi, he was dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遇赦當還故官。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, a general amnesty entitled him to return to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, a general amnesty entitled him to return to his former post.

sentences.zh: 帝以諤前在湖廣頗摭楚王細故，謫海鹽知縣。

translations.literal: The emperor, because E had formerly in Huguang seized on petty grievances against the Prince of Chu, demoted him to magistrate of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because E had formerly in Huguang seized on petty grievances against the Prince of Chu, demoted him to magistrate of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 遷荊王長史，為王府所厭苦。

translations.literal: He was moved to Chief Secretary to the Prince of Jing, where the princely household wearied of him and made him miserable.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Chief Secretary to the Prince of Jing, where the princely household wearied of him and made his life miserable.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年遷鎮江同知。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande he was transferred to Vice-Prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 3 he was transferred to Vice-Prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 致仕歸，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and returned home, then died.

sentences.zh: 戴綸，高密人。

translations.literal: Dai Lun was a native of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Lun was a native of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，自昌邑訓導擢禮科給事中，與編修林長懋俱侍皇太孫說書。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era, from instructor at Changyi he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites, and together with Compiler Lin Changmao both lectured the emperor's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle era, from instructor at Changyi he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Rites, and together with Compiler Lin Changmao both lectured the emperor's grandson.

sentences.zh: 歷中允、諭德。

translations.literal: He passed through vice-director and preceptor posts.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through vice-director and preceptor posts.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，太孫為太子，遷洗馬，仍侍講讀。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne the grandson became crown prince; Lun was moved to Groom of the Heir Apparent yet still lectured and read with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne the grandson became crown prince; Lun was moved to Groom of the Heir Apparent yet still lectured and read with him.

sentences.zh: 始成祖命太孫習武事，太孫亦雅好之，時出騎射。

translations.literal: At first Chengzu had ordered the grandson to study military affairs; the grandson also took a keen liking to them and would often go out riding and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chengzu had ordered the grandson to study military affairs; the grandson also took a keen liking to them and would often go out riding and shooting.

sentences.zh: 綸與長懋以太孫春秋方富，不宜荒學問而事遊畋，時時進諫。

translations.literal: Lun and Changmao, because the grandson was in the prime of youth, held that he should not neglect learning for hunting and sport, and repeatedly admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and Changmao, because the grandson was in the prime of youth, held that he should not neglect learning for hunting and sport, and repeatedly admonished him.

sentences.zh: 綸又具疏為帝言之。

translations.literal: Lun also drew up a memorial in full and reported it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Lun also drew up a memorial in full and reported it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 他日，太孫侍，帝問：「宮臣相得者誰也？」

translations.literal: Another day, as the grandson attended, the emperor asked: "Which of your palace officers get along with you?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day, as the grandson attended, the emperor asked: "Which of your palace officers get along with you?"

sentences.zh: 太孫以綸對。

translations.literal: The grandson named Lun.
translations.idiomatic: The grandson named Lun.

sentences.zh: 因出綸奏付之，太孫由此怨綸。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore produced Lun's memorial and gave it to him; from this the grandson bore a grudge against Lun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore produced Lun's memorial and gave it to him; from this the grandson bore a grudge against Lun.

sentences.zh: 長懋者，莆田人。

translations.literal: As for Changmao, he was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: As for Changmao, he was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 以鄉薦歷青州教授，擢編修。

translations.literal: Through the provincial recommendation he served as instructor at Qingzhou, then was promoted to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Through the provincial recommendation he served as instructor at Qingzhou, then was promoted to Compiler.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初，進中允。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renzong's reign he was advanced to vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Renzong's reign he was advanced to vice-director.

sentences.zh: 為人剛嚴，累進直言，與綸善。

translations.literal: By nature stern and severe, he repeatedly offered blunt counsel and was on good terms with Lun.
translations.idiomatic: In character he was stern and severe; he repeatedly offered blunt counsel and was close to Lun.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，加恩宮僚，擢綸兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, he extended favor to the palace staff and promoted Lun to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, he extended favor to the palace staff and promoted Lun to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復以諫獵忤旨，命參贊交阯軍務。

translations.literal: Before long, for again remonstrating against hunting contrary to the imperial will, he was ordered to assist in Jiaozhi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, for again remonstrating against hunting contrary to the imperial will, he was ordered to assist in Jiaozhi military affairs.

sentences.zh: 而長懋自南京來，後至，亦出為郁林知州。

translations.literal: Changmao came from Nanjing and arrived later; he too was sent out as prefect of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Changmao came from Nanjing and arrived later; he too was sent out as prefect of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 無何，坐怨望，並逮至京，下錦衣衛獄。

translations.literal: Before long, on a charge of harboring resentment, both were seized and brought to the capital and sent to the Embroidered Uniform Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on a charge of harboring resentment, both were seized, brought to the capital, and imprisoned in the Embroidered Uniform Guard jail.

sentences.zh: 帝臨鞫之，綸抗辯，觸帝怒，立箠死，籍其家。

translations.literal: The emperor personally interrogated them; Lun argued back, provoking the emperor's wrath, and was immediately beaten to death; his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally interrogated them; Lun argued back, provoking the emperor's wrath, and was immediately beaten to death; his household goods were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 諸父河南知府賢、太僕寺卿希文皆被系。

translations.literal: His uncles Xian, Prefect of Henan, and Xiwen, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, were also imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles Xian, Prefect of Henan, and Xiwen, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, were also imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 而長懋在獄十年，英宗立，乃得釋。

translations.literal: But Changmao was in prison ten years; when Yingzong took the throne, he was finally released.
translations.idiomatic: Changmao had been in prison ten years; only when Yingzong took the throne was he at last released.

sentences.zh: 復其官，還守郁林，有惠政。

translations.literal: His office was restored, and he returned to serve as prefect of Yulin, where he governed with benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: His office was restored; he returned to govern Yulin as prefect and won a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，州人立廟祀之。

translations.literal: When he died, the people of the prefecture erected a temple to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the people of the prefecture erected a temple in his honor.

sentences.zh: 陳祚，字永錫，吳人。

translations.literal: Chen Zuo, styled Yongxi, was a native of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zuo, styled Yongxi, was a native of Wu.

sentences.zh: 永樂中進士。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era he passed the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign he passed the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 擢河南參議。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Administrative Vice Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Administrative Vice Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 十五年與布政使周文褒、王文振合疏，言建都北京非便，並謫均州太和山佃戶。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, together with Administrative Commissioners Zhou Wenbao and Wang Wenzhen, he submitted a joint memorial saying that making Beijing the capital was inexpedient; all were banished as tenant farmers on Mount Taihe in Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15, together with Administrative Commissioners Zhou Wenbao and Wang Wenzhen, he submitted a joint memorial arguing that establishing Beijing as the capital was inexpedient; all three were banished as tenant farmers on Mount Taihe in Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 躬耕力作，處之晏然。

translations.literal: He farmed with his own hands and bore the situation with composure.
translations.idiomatic: He farmed with his own hands and bore his exile with composure.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，詔選用遷謫諸臣，祚在選中。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, an edict ordered that banished officials be selected for reuse; Zuo was among those chosen.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, an edict called for the reuse of banished officials, and Zuo was among those selected.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，不果用。

translations.literal: But the emperor died before the appointment could take effect.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor died before he could be appointed.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年命憲臣即均州群試之，祚策第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande the emperor ordered judicial officials to hold a group examination at Junzhou; Zuo's policy essay ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 2 the emperor ordered judicial officials to hold a group examination at Junzhou; Zuo's policy essay ranked first.

sentences.zh: 試吏部，復第一。

translations.literal: Tested by the Ministry of Personnel, he again ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: When examined by the Ministry of Personnel, he again ranked first.

sentences.zh: 遂擢御史，巡按福建。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to Censor and sent to inspect Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Censor and dispatched to inspect Fujian.

sentences.zh: 方面大吏多被彈擊，禁止和買，閩人德之。

translations.literal: Many high provincial officials were impeached; he forbade compulsory government purchases, and the people of Min were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Many senior provincial officials were impeached; he forbade compulsory government purchases, and the people of Fujian were grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 還奏白塔河上通邵伯湖，下註大江，蘇、松舟楫，多從往來，淺狹湮塞，請開浚。

translations.literal: On his return he memorialized that the Baita River connected with Lake Shaobo and emptied into the great river; boats from Suzhou and Songjiang often traveled that route, but the channel was shallow, narrow, and silted, and he asked that it be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he memorialized that the Baita River connected with Lake Shaobo and emptied into the Yangzi; boats from Suzhou and Songjiang often used the route, but the channel was shallow, narrow, and silted, and he requested dredging.

sentences.zh: 從之，轉漕果便。

translations.literal: The request was approved, and grain transport by water proved convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved, and grain transport by water became genuinely convenient.

sentences.zh: 尋出按江西。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was sent out to inspect Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was sent out to inspect Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平，帝頗事遊獵玩好。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was at peace, but the emperor was much given to hunting and curios.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm was at peace, yet the emperor was much given to hunting and curios.

sentences.zh: 祚馳疏勸勤聖學。

translations.literal: Zuo sent an urgent memorial urging diligent pursuit of sacred learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo sent an urgent memorial urging the emperor to pursue sacred learning diligently.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「帝王之學先明理，明理在讀書。

translations.literal: In summary it said: "The learning of emperors and kings begins with clarifying principle, and clarifying principle lies in reading books.
translations.idiomatic: In summary it said: "The learning of emperors and kings begins with clarifying principle, and clarifying principle lies in reading books.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖有聖德，而經筵未甚興舉，講學未有程度，聖賢精微，古今治亂，豈能周知洞晰？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, though possessed of sacred virtue, has not greatly revived the classics lecture hall; lecturing and study have not reached a settled level—how can the subtle words of sages and worthies and the patterns of order and chaos through the ages be thoroughly known and clearly understood?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, though possessed of sacred virtue, has not greatly revived the classics lecture hall; lecturing and study have not reached a settled level—how then can the subtle doctrines of sages and worthies and the patterns of order and chaos through the ages be thoroughly known and clearly understood?

sentences.zh: 真德秀《大學衍義》一書，聖賢格言，無不畢載。

translations.literal: In Zhen Dexiu's book Daxue yanyi, the maxims of sages and worthies are all fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhen Dexiu's Daxue yanyi, the maxims of sages and worthies are all fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 願於聽政之暇，命儒臣講說，非有大故，無得間斷。

translations.literal: I beg that in the leisure after hearing government affairs Your Majesty order Confucian officials to lecture on it, and that except for great cause there be no interruption.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that in the leisure after hearing government affairs Your Majesty order Confucian officials to lecture on it, and that except for grave cause there be no interruption.

sentences.zh: 使知古今若何而治，政事若何而得。

translations.literal: Then one will know how the past was governed and how government affairs are rightly conducted.
translations.idiomatic: Then one will know how the past was governed and how government affairs are rightly conducted.

sentences.zh: 必能開廣聰明，增光德業。

translations.literal: Surely intelligence will be broadened and virtue and achievement increased.
translations.idiomatic: Surely intelligence will be broadened and virtue and achievement increased.

sentences.zh: 而邪佞之以奇巧蕩聖心者自見疏遠，天下人民受福無窮矣。」

translations.literal: And those wicked and fawning men who would shake the sacred mind with strange artifices will of themselves be kept at a distance, and the people of the realm will receive boundless blessing."
translations.idiomatic: And those wicked and fawning men who would shake the sacred mind with strange artifices will of themselves be kept at a distance, and the people of the realm will receive boundless blessing."

sentences.zh: 帝見疏大怒曰：「豎儒謂朕未讀《大學》耶！

translations.literal: When the emperor saw the memorial he was greatly enraged and said: "Does this petty scholar think I have not read the Daxue!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw the memorial he was greatly enraged and said: "Does this petty scholar think I have not read the Daxue!

sentences.zh: 薄朕至此，不可不誅。」

translations.literal: To slight me to this degree cannot go unpunished."
translations.idiomatic: To slight me to this degree cannot go unpunished."

sentences.zh: 學士陳循頓首曰：「俗士處遠，不知上無書不讀也。」

translations.literal: Academician Chen Xun kowtowed and said: "A vulgar scholar far from court does not know that Your Majesty reads every book."
translations.idiomatic: Academician Chen Xun kowtowed and said: "A vulgar scholar far from court does not know that Your Majesty reads every book."

sentences.zh: 帝意稍解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 下祚獄，逮其家人十餘口，隔別禁系者五年，其父竟瘐死。

translations.literal: Zuo was sent to prison; more than ten members of his household were seized, and for five years they were held separately under detention; his father died of illness in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was sent to prison; more than ten members of his household were seized, and for five years they were held separately under detention; his father died of illness in confinement.

sentences.zh: 其時，刑部主事郭循諫拓西內皇城修離宮，逮入面詰之。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Xun, a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, remonstrated against expanding the inner quarters of the western imperial city to build a detached palace; he was seized and brought in for a face-to-face interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guo Xun, a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, remonstrated against expanding the inner quarters of the western imperial city to build a detached palace; he was seized and brought in for a face-to-face interrogation.

sentences.zh: 循抗辯不屈，亦下獄。

translations.literal: Xun argued back without yielding and was also imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xun argued back without yielding and was also imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，祚與循皆得釋復官。

translations.literal: When Yingzong took the throne, both Zuo and Xun were released and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong took the throne, both Zuo and Xun were released and restored to office.

sentences.zh: 祚再按湖廣。

translations.literal: Zuo again inspected Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo again inspected Huguang.

sentences.zh: 以奏遼王貴烚罪有所隱，與巡撫侍郎吳政逮至京，下獄。

translations.literal: Because in memorializing the crimes of Prince of Liao Guiyan he had concealed something, he was arrested together with Grand Coordinator and Vice Minister Wu Zheng and brought to the capital, then imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Because in memorializing the crimes of Prince of Liao Zhu Guiyan he had concealed something, he was arrested together with Grand Coordinator and Vice Minister Wu Zheng and brought to the capital, then imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 尋赦出。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 時王振用事，法務嚴峻，祚上言：「乃者法司論獄，多違定律。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zhen was in power and legal practice was severe; Zuo memorialized: "Recently when the judicial offices tried cases, they often violated the code.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Zhen was in power and legal practice was severe; Zuo memorialized: "Recently when the judicial offices tried cases, they often violated the code.

sentences.zh: 如侍郎吳璽誤舉主事吳軏，宜坐貢舉非其人律，乃坐以奏事有規避律斬。

translations.literal: For example, Vice Minister Wu Xi mistakenly recommended Secretary Wu Yue; he should have been charged under the statute on recommending an unfit person, yet he was sentenced to decapitation under the statute on memorializing with evasion.
translations.idiomatic: For example, Vice Minister Wu Xi mistakenly recommended Secretary Wu Yue; he should have been charged under the statute on recommending an unfit person, yet he was sentenced to decapitation under the statute on memorializing with evasion.

sentences.zh: 及軏自經死，獄官獄卒罪應遞減，乃援不應為重罪，概杖之。

translations.literal: When Yue hanged himself, the crimes of prison officials and guards should have been reduced in degree, yet they invoked the heavy crime of doing what ought not to be done and were all beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue hanged himself, the crimes of prison officials and guards should have been reduced in degree, yet they invoked the heavy crime of doing what ought not to be done and were all beaten with the staff.

sentences.zh: 一事如此，余可推矣。

translations.literal: When one matter is like this, the rest may be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: When one matter is like this, the rest may be inferred.

sentences.zh: 天時不順，災沴數見，未必非此。」

translations.literal: Heaven's seasons are out of order and calamities appear repeatedly—this may well be the cause."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's seasons are out of order and calamities appear repeatedly—this may well be the cause."

sentences.zh: 帝是之，以其章示法司。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and showed his memorial to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and showed his memorial to the judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 尋改南京，遷福建按察使僉事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Nanjing, then promoted to Vice Commissioner in the Fujian Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Nanjing, then promoted to Vice Commissioner in the Fujian Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 有威惠，神祠不載祀典者悉撤去。

translations.literal: He had both authority and kindness; shrines not recorded in the sacrificial statutes were all removed.
translations.idiomatic: He combined authority with kindness; shrines not recorded in the sacrificial statutes were all removed.

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾歸，卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned home on account of illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he returned home on account of illness and died.

sentences.zh: 祚天資嚴毅，雖子弟罕接其言笑，獨重里人邢量。

translations.literal: Zuo was stern and severe by nature; even his own kin rarely heard him jest, yet he greatly esteemed his fellow townsman Xing Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was stern and severe by nature; even his own kin rarely heard him jest, yet he greatly esteemed his fellow townsman Xing Liang.

sentences.zh: 量博學士，隱於卜，敝屋數椽，或竟日不舉火。

translations.literal: Liang was a learned scholar who lived in seclusion as a diviner; he had only a few rafters of a dilapidated house and sometimes went a whole day without lighting a fire.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was a learned scholar who lived in seclusion as a diviner; he had only a few rafters of a dilapidated house and sometimes went a whole day without lighting a fire.

sentences.zh: 祚數挾冊就質疑，往往至暮。

translations.literal: Zuo often carried books to him with questions and would stay until evening.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo often carried books to him with questions and would stay until evening.

sentences.zh: 郭循，字循初，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Guo Xun, styled Xunchu, was a native of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun, styled Xunchu, was a native of Luling.

sentences.zh: 居官有才譽。

translations.literal: In office he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In office he had a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 既復職，進郎中，以尚書魏源薦，擢廣東參政，有剿寇功。

translations.literal: After his restoration he was advanced to Director; on the recommendation of Minister Wei Yuan he was promoted to Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong and had merit in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After his restoration he was advanced to Director; on the recommendation of Minister Wei Yuan he was promoted to Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong and had merit in suppressing bandits.

sentences.zh: 景泰初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Jingtai reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 劉球，字廷振，安福人。

translations.literal: Liu Qiu, styled Tingzhen, was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu, styled Tingzhen, was a native of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 永樂十九年進士。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yongle he passed the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 19 he passed the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 家居讀書十年，從學者甚眾。

translations.literal: He stayed home reading books for ten years, and those who studied under him were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed home reading books for ten years, and those who studied under him were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 授禮部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 胡濙薦侍經筵，與修《宣宗實錄》，改翰林侍講。

translations.literal: Hu Ying recommended him to attend the classics lecture; he helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong and was transferred to Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying recommended him to attend the classics lecture; he helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong and was transferred to Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 從弟比知莆田，遺一夏布。

translations.literal: His younger cousin, serving as magistrate of Putian, sent him a length of summer cloth.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin, serving as magistrate of Putian, sent him a length of summer cloth.

sentences.zh: 球封還，貽書戒之。

translations.literal: Qiu sealed it and returned it, sending a letter to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu sealed it and returned it, sending a letter to admonish him.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，帝以王振言，大舉征麓川。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong, on Wang Zhen's advice, the emperor launched a great campaign against Luchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 6, on Wang Zhen's advice, the emperor launched a great campaign against Luchuan.

sentences.zh: 球上疏曰：

translations.literal: Qiu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qiu submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 帝王之馭四裔，必宥其小而防其大。

translations.literal: In governing the four borderlands, emperors and kings must pardon the small and guard against the great.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the four borderlands, emperors and kings must pardon the small and guard against the great.

sentences.zh: 所以適緩急之宜，為天下久安計也。

translations.literal: This is how to suit the pace of urgency and ease and plan for long peace under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This is how to suit the pace of urgency and ease and plan for lasting peace under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 周伐崇不克，退修德教以待其降。

translations.literal: When Zhou attacked Chong and could not overcome it, they withdrew to cultivate virtue and teaching and await its surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou attacked Chong and could not overcome it, they withdrew to cultivate virtue and teaching and await its surrender.

sentences.zh: 至於玁狁，則命南仲城朔方以備之。

translations.literal: As for the Xianyun, they ordered Nan Zhong to fortify Shuofang to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Xianyun, they ordered Nan Zhong to fortify Shuofang to guard against them.

sentences.zh: 漢征南越不利，即罷兵賜書通好。

translations.literal: When Han campaigned against Nanyue without success, they at once ceased troops and sent letters to open friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: When Han campaigned against Nanyue without success, they at once ceased troops and sent letters to open friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 至於匈奴，雖已和親，猶募民徙居塞下，入粟實邊，復命魏尚守雲中拒之。

translations.literal: As for the Xiongnu, though there was already a marriage alliance, they still recruited people to move and settle below the passes, sent grain to fill the border, and again ordered Wei Shang to hold Yunzhong and repel them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Xiongnu, though there was already a marriage alliance, they still recruited people to move and settle below the passes, sent grain to fill the border, and again ordered Wei Shang to hold Yunzhong and repel them.

sentences.zh: 今麓川殘寇思任發素本羈屬，以邊將失馭，致勤大兵。

translations.literal: Today the remnant bandits of Luchuan, Si Renfa, were originally a subordinate dependency; because border generals lost control, a great army was stirred up.
translations.idiomatic: Today the remnant bandits of Luchuan, Si Renfa, were originally a subordinate dependency; because border generals lost control, a great army was stirred up.

sentences.zh: 雖渠魁未殲，亦多戮群醜，為誅為舍，無系輕重。

translations.literal: Though the chief culprit has not yet been destroyed, many of the villainous host have already been killed; whether to execute or spare should not be tied to weight or lightness.
translations.idiomatic: Though the chief culprit has not yet been destroyed, many of the villainous host have already been killed; whether to execute or spare should not be tied to weight or lightness.

sentences.zh: 璽書原其罪釁，使得自新，甚盛德也。

translations.literal: The imperial letter pardoned his crimes and faults and allowed him to renew himself—this was very great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial letter pardoned his crimes and faults and allowed him to renew himself—this was very great virtue.

sentences.zh: 邊將不達聖意，復議大舉。

translations.literal: Border generals did not grasp the sacred intent and again proposed a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Border generals did not grasp the sacred intent and again proposed a great campaign.

sentences.zh: 欲屯十二萬眾於雲南，以趣其降，不降則攻之。

translations.literal: They wished to station one hundred twenty thousand men in Yunnan to press for surrender, and if he did not surrender, to attack.
translations.idiomatic: They wished to station one hundred twenty thousand men in Yunnan to press for surrender, and if he did not surrender, to attack.

sentences.zh: 不慮王師不可輕出，蠻性不可驟馴，地險不可用眾，客兵不可久淹。

translations.literal: They did not consider that the royal army must not be lightly sent forth, that barbarian nature cannot be quickly tamed, that dangerous terrain cannot employ great numbers, and that guest troops cannot long be detained.
translations.idiomatic: They did not consider that the royal army must not be lightly sent forth, that barbarian nature cannot be quickly tamed, that dangerous terrain cannot employ great numbers, and that guest troops cannot long be detained.

sentences.zh: 況南方水旱相仍，軍民交困，若復動眾，紛擾為憂。

translations.literal: Moreover, south of the Yangzi flood and drought follow one another, army and people alike are distressed; if troops are stirred again, turmoil will be the worry.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, south of the Yangzi flood and drought follow one another, army and people alike are distressed; if troops are stirred again, turmoil will be the worry.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂宜緩天誅，如周、漢之於崇、越也。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say that Heaven's punishment should be slowed, as Zhou and Han did toward Chong and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures to say that Heaven's punishment should be slowed, as Zhou and Han did toward Chong and Yue.

sentences.zh: 至於瓦剌，終為邊患。

translations.literal: As for the Oirats, in the end they will be a border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Oirats, in the end they will be a border trouble.

sentences.zh: 及其未即騷動，正宜以時防禦。

translations.literal: Before they have yet stirred to disorder, it is precisely the time to defend against them in season.
translations.idiomatic: Before they have yet stirred to disorder, it is precisely the time to defend against them in season.

sentences.zh: 乃欲移甘肅守將以事南征，卒然有警，何以為禦？

translations.literal: Yet they wish to shift the garrison commander of Gansu to the southern campaign; if alarm suddenly arises, how will we defend?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they wish to shift the garrison commander of Gansu to the southern campaign; if alarm suddenly arises, how will we defend?

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為宜慎防遏，如周、漢之於玁狁、匈奴也。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to think that careful defense and restraint are fitting, as Zhou and Han toward the Xianyun and Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures to think that careful defense and restraint are fitting, as Zhou and Han toward the Xianyun and Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下罷大舉之議。

translations.literal: I bow and hope Your Majesty will abandon the proposal for a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: I bow and hope Your Majesty will abandon the proposal for a great campaign.

sentences.zh: 推選智謀將帥，輔以才識大臣，量調官軍，分屯金齒諸要害。

translations.literal: Select wise and resourceful generals, assist them with talented and discerning ministers, measure and deploy official troops, and station them in divisions at the key points such as Jinchi.
translations.idiomatic: Select wise and resourceful generals, assist them with talented and discerning ministers, measure and deploy official troops, and station them in divisions at the key points such as Jinchi.

sentences.zh: 結木邦諸蠻以為援，乘間進攻，因便撫諭，寇自可服。

translations.literal: Win the support of the various barbarians of Mubang as allies; seize the opportunity to attack, and meanwhile offer convenient reassurance and instruction—the bandits will of themselves submit.
translations.idiomatic: Win the support of the various barbarians of Mubang as allies; seize the opportunity to attack, and meanwhile offer convenient reassurance and instruction—the bandits will of themselves submit.

sentences.zh: 至於西北障塞，當敕邊臣巡視。

translations.literal: As for the northwestern barriers and passes, border officials should be ordered to inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the northwestern barriers and passes, border officials should be ordered to inspect them.

sentences.zh: 浚築溝垣，增繕城堡，勤訓練，嚴守望，以防不虞，有備無患之道也。

translations.literal: Dredge and build ditches and walls, add and repair castles, train diligently, keep watch strictly, and guard against the unforeseen—this is the way to have preparation and no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Dredge and build ditches and walls, add and repair castles, train diligently, keep watch strictly, and guard against the unforeseen—this is the way to have preparation and no worry.

sentences.zh: 章下兵部。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 謂南征已有成命，不用球言。

translations.literal: They said the southern campaign already had a settled command and Qiu's words were not used.
translations.idiomatic: They said the southern campaign already had a settled command and Qiu's words were not used.

sentences.zh: 八年五月雷震奉天殿。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year, lightning struck the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year, lightning struck the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 球應詔上言所宜先者十事。

translations.literal: Qiu, responding to the edict, memorialized the ten matters that should come first.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu, responding to the edict, memorialized the ten matters that should come first.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: In summary:
translations.idiomatic: In summary:

sentences.zh: 古聖王不作無益，故心正而天不違之。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings did nothing without benefit; therefore the mind was correct and Heaven did not oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sage kings did nothing without benefit; therefore the mind was correct and Heaven did not oppose them.

sentences.zh: 臣願皇上勤禦經筵，數進儒臣，講求至道。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that Your Majesty diligently attend the classics lecture, frequently advance Confucian officials, and seek the ultimate Way.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes that Your Majesty diligently attend the classics lecture, frequently advance Confucian officials, and seek the ultimate Way.

sentences.zh: 務使學問功至，理欲判然，則聖心正而天心自順。

translations.literal: See to it that learning and effort reach completion and principle and desire are clearly distinguished; then the sacred mind will be correct and the mind of Heaven will of itself accord.
translations.idiomatic: See to it that learning and effort reach completion and principle and desire are clearly distinguished; then the sacred mind will be correct and the mind of Heaven will of itself accord.

sentences.zh: 夫政由已出，則權不下移。

translations.literal: When government proceeds from oneself, power does not shift downward.
translations.idiomatic: When government proceeds from oneself, power does not shift downward.

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗日視三朝，時召大臣於便殿裁決庶政，權歸總於上。

translations.literal: Taizu and Taizong viewed court three times daily and at times summoned ministers to the side hall to decide ordinary government; power was gathered at the top.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Taizong viewed court three times daily and at times summoned ministers to the side hall to decide ordinary government; power was gathered at the top.

sentences.zh: 皇上臨御九年，事體日熟。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ruled nine years and matters are daily more familiar.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ruled nine years and matters are daily more familiar.

sentences.zh: 願守二聖成規，復親決故事，使權歸於一。

translations.literal: I wish that you keep the established rules of the two sages, restore personal decision of precedent affairs, and let power return to one.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that you keep the established rules of the two sages, restore personal decision of precedent affairs, and let power return to one.

sentences.zh: 古之擇大臣者，必詢諸左右、大夫、國人。

translations.literal: In antiquity, in choosing great ministers one surely consulted those at left and right, the grandees, and the people of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, in choosing great ministers one surely consulted those at left and right, the grandees, and the people of the state.

sentences.zh: 及其有犯，雖至大辟亦不加刑，第賜之死。

translations.literal: When they had offenses, even if it reached the great punishment, no additional penalty was imposed—only death was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When they had offenses, even if it reached the great punishment, no additional penalty was imposed—only death was bestowed.

sentences.zh: 今用大臣未嘗皆出公論。

translations.literal: Now those employed as great ministers have not all emerged from public consensus.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers appointed today are not always chosen on the basis of broad public approval.

sentences.zh: 及有小失，輒桎梏箠楚之；

translations.literal: When they commit small faults, they are immediately shackled and beaten with the cudgel;
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest misstep they are shackled and flogged;

sentences.zh: 然未幾時，又復其職。

translations.literal: yet before long they are restored to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: yet within a short time they are returned to office.

sentences.zh: 甚非所以待大臣也。

translations.literal: This is very much not the way to treat great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: This is no way to treat senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 自今擇任大臣，宜允愜眾論。

translations.literal: From now on, in selecting and appointing great ministers, one should allow and satisfy public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, in choosing ministers, Your Majesty should heed widely shared consensus.

sentences.zh: 小犯則置之。

translations.literal: For minor offenses, let them be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Minor transgressions should be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 果不可容，下法司定罪，使自為計。

translations.literal: If truly they cannot be tolerated, send them down to the judicial offices to determine guilt and let them arrange matters for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If punishment is truly warranted, refer the case to the judicial authorities for sentencing and let the offender answer for himself.

sentences.zh: 勿輒系，庶不乖共天職之意。

translations.literal: Do not casually imprison them; then one may not violate the intent of sharing Heaven's charge.
translations.idiomatic: Do not casually throw them in chains, so as not to betray the spirit of ministers jointly bearing Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 今之太常，即古之秩宗，必得清慎習禮之臣，然後可交神明。

translations.literal: Today's Director of Ceremonial is the ancient Director of Ancestral Rites; one must obtain officials who are pure, cautious, and practiced in ritual—only then can one communicate with the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The present Court of Imperial Rites corresponds to the ancient office of Director of Ancestral Rites; only officials of integrity, discretion, and ritual mastery can serve as intermediaries with the divine.

sentences.zh: 今卿貳皆缺，宜選擇儒臣，使領其職。

translations.literal: Now the assistant directors are all vacant; one should select Confucian officials and have them lead these posts.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy directorships are now all unfilled; scholar-officials should be chosen to fill them.

sentences.zh: 古者省方巡狩，所以察吏得失，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: In antiquity, inspecting the regions and touring on hunts were for examining officials' gains and losses and inquiring into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times emperors toured the realm to assess official conduct and learn of popular suffering.

sentences.zh: 兩漢、唐、宋盛時，數遣使巡行郡縣，洪、永間亦嘗行之。

translations.literal: At the height of the Two Han, Tang, and Song, envoys were repeatedly sent to inspect commanderies and counties; under Hongwu and Yongle this was also once carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, imperial commissioners were repeatedly sent to tour the prefectures and counties; the Hongwu and Yongle reigns saw the practice as well.

sentences.zh: 今久不舉，故吏多貪虐，民不聊生，而軍衛尤甚。

translations.literal: Now it has long not been undertaken, so officials are many in greed and cruelty, the people cannot sustain life, and among the garrison guards it is especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: The practice has long been abandoned, with the result that officials are often corrupt and cruel, the people can barely survive, and conditions in the garrisons are worst of all.

sentences.zh: 宜擇公明廉幹之臣，分行天下。

translations.literal: One should select officials who are fair, discerning, honest, and capable, and dispatch them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Fair, incorruptible, and capable officials should be chosen and sent throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 古人君不親刑獄，必付理官，蓋恐徇喜怒而有所輕重也。

translations.literal: In antiquity rulers did not personally handle criminal cases; they always entrusted them to judicial officials, fearing lest they follow personal pleasure and anger and thereby show partiality in severity or leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sovereigns did not personally try criminal cases but left them to the judiciary, lest judgment be swayed by personal favor or wrath.

sentences.zh: 邇法司所上獄，多奉敕增減輕重，法司不能執奏。

translations.literal: Recently the cases submitted by the judicial offices are mostly altered in severity according to edict; the judicial offices cannot uphold and memorialize their views.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the judicial bureaus' sentencing recommendations are frequently overridden by imperial edict; the courts dare not insist on their judgments.

sentences.zh: 及訊他囚，又觀望以為輕重，民用多冤。

translations.literal: When interrogating other prisoners, they again watch and wait to determine severity or leniency, and among the people there is much injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When trying other cases they merely watch for cues about what penalty to impose, and the common people suffer many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 宜使各舉其職。

translations.literal: One should have each perform his own duty.
translations.idiomatic: Each office should be allowed to discharge its proper function.

sentences.zh: 至運磚輸米諸例，均非古法，尤宜罷之。

translations.literal: As for such precedents as transporting bricks and conveying rice, none are ancient law and above all should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Practices such as requiring convicts to haul bricks and transport grain are nowhere found in ancient law and should be abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》營築悉書，戒勞民也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records every construction project as a warning against burdening the people with labor.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records every construction project as an admonition against overworking the populace.

sentences.zh: 京師興作五六年矣，曰「不煩民而役軍」，軍獨非國家赤子乎？

translations.literal: Construction in the capital has gone on five or six years; they say 'we do not trouble the people but employ the army'—are soldiers alone not the nation's beloved children?
translations.idiomatic: Building projects in the capital have dragged on for five or six years, with officials claiming they 'burden the civilians not but only use the army'—yet are soldiers not also the emperor's own cherished subjects?

sentences.zh: 況營作多完，宜罷工以蘇其力。

translations.literal: Moreover, much construction is already finished; work should be halted so their strength may recover.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, most of the projects are already complete; construction should cease so the laborers may recover their strength.

sentences.zh: 各處水旱，有司既不振救，請減租稅，或亦徒事虛文。

translations.literal: In various places flood and drought—since the responsible officials neither relieve nor rescue, when petitions to reduce rent and tax are made, these too are sometimes merely empty formalities.
translations.idiomatic: When flood and drought strike the provinces, local officials fail to provide relief, and petitions to cut taxes often produce nothing but empty paperwork.

sentences.zh: 宜令戶部以時振濟，量加減免，使不致失業。

translations.literal: One should order the Ministry of Revenue to give timely relief, measure out increases in reduction and remission, and ensure people do not lose their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue should be instructed to provide timely relief and measured tax reductions so that people are not ruined.

sentences.zh: 麓川連年用兵，死者十七八，軍貲爵賞不可勝計。

translations.literal: Luchuan has seen military use year after year; seventy or eighty percent have died; military expenses and enfeoffments and rewards cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Years of war in Luchuan have left seven or eight men in ten dead; the cost in supplies, titles, and rewards is beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 今又遣蔣貴遠征緬甸，責獻思任發。

translations.literal: Now Jiang Gui is again sent on distant expedition to Burma to demand the surrender of Si Renfa.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gui has now been dispatched on a far campaign into Burma to demand that Si Renfa be delivered up.

sentences.zh: 果擒以歸，不過梟諸通衢而已。

translations.literal: If he is truly captured and brought back, it will amount to no more than displaying his head at a public thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he is captured and brought back, the outcome would be nothing more than displaying his severed head in the streets.

sentences.zh: 緬將挾以為功，必求與木邦共分其地。

translations.literal: The Burmese general will seize this as merit and surely demand to divide the territory with Mubang.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese commanders will use the capture to claim credit and insist on dividing the territory with Mubang.

sentences.zh: 不與則致怒，與之則兩蠻坐大，是減一麓川生二麓川也。

translations.literal: If not granted, they will become angry; if granted, the two barbarians will sit and grow great—this is reducing one Luchuan and producing two Luchuans.
translations.idiomatic: Refuse them and they will turn hostile; grant their demand and both tribal powers will grow—replacing one Luchuan with two.

sentences.zh: 設有蹉跎，兵事無已。

translations.literal: Suppose there is delay; military affairs will have no end.
translations.idiomatic: Any setback would keep the war going indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 臣見皇上每錄重囚，多宥令從軍，仁心若此。

translations.literal: Your subject has seen that Your Majesty, each time recording serious prisoners, often pardons them and orders them to serve in the army—such is your benevolent heart.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen Your Majesty repeatedly pardon condemned criminals and send them to serve in the army—such is Your compassion.

sentences.zh: 今欲生得一失地之竄寇，而驅數萬無罪之眾以就死地，豈不有乖於好生之仁哉？

translations.literal: Now you wish to capture alive a fugitive bandit who has lost his territory, yet drive tens of thousands of innocent people toward the place of death—does this not depart from the benevolence of cherishing life?
translations.idiomatic: To capture one fugitive chieftain who has already lost his domain, while driving tens of thousands of innocent men toward their deaths—is this not at odds with Your humane regard for life?

sentences.zh: 況思機發已嘗遣人來貢，非無悔過乞免之意。

translations.literal: Moreover, Si Jifa has already once sent envoys to offer tribute; it is not that he lacks intention to repent and beg exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Si Jifa has already sent tribute missions, showing that he wishes to repent and sue for pardon.

sentences.zh: 若敕緬斬任發首來獻，仍敕思機發盡削四境之地，分於各寨新附之蠻，則一方可寧矣。

translations.literal: If an edict orders Burma to cut off Renfa's head and present it, and still orders Si Jifa to fully strip the territory on all four borders and divide it among the newly submitted barbarian stockades of each district, then one region can be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Order Burma to deliver Si Renfa's head, and command Si Jifa to surrender all border territories to be distributed among the newly submitted tribal chiefs—then the region could at last be pacified.

sentences.zh: 迤北貢使日增，包藏禍心，誠為難測。

translations.literal: Tribute envoys from the northern frontier daily increase; they conceal harmful intent and are truly hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Tributary missions from the northern frontier grow more numerous by the day; their designs are hidden and truly impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 宜分遣給事、御史閱視京邊官軍，及時訓練，勿使借工各廠，服役私家。

translations.literal: One should separately dispatch supervising secretaries and censors to inspect the capital-border garrison troops, train them in timely fashion, and not allow them to borrow work at the various factories or serve private households.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors should be dispatched to inspect capital and frontier troops, ensure they are trained promptly, and prevent them from being lent out to factories or private households.

sentences.zh: 公武舉之選以求良將，定召募之法以來武勇。

translations.literal: Open the military examination selection to seek good generals; fix recruitment methods to attract martial valor.
translations.idiomatic: Military examinations should be held openly to find able commanders, and conscription rules set to draw in the brave.

sentences.zh: 廣屯田，公鹽法，以厚儲蓄。

translations.literal: Expand military colonies; make the salt laws public and uniform; thereby enrich stored reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Expand frontier farming colonies and standardize the salt monopoly to strengthen government reserves.

sentences.zh: 庶武備無缺，而外患有防。

translations.literal: Then perhaps military preparedness will lack nothing and external troubles will have defense.
translations.idiomatic: Thus defenses would be kept in readiness and external threats held in check.

sentences.zh: 疏入，下廷議。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; it was sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the court was ordered to deliberate on it.

sentences.zh: 言球所奏，惟擇太常官宜從，令吏部推舉。

translations.literal: It was said that of what Qiu memorialized, only the selection of Ceremonial officials should be followed; the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to recommend candidates.
translations.idiomatic: The court ruled that of Qiu's recommendations, only the proposal to fill posts in the Court of Imperial Rites should be adopted, and the Ministry of Personnel was instructed to nominate suitable candidates.

sentences.zh: 修撰董璘遂乞改官太常，奉享祀事。

translations.literal: Compiler Dong Lin thereupon petitioned to change his post to Ceremonial, to perform sacrificial duties.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Dong Lin then requested a transfer to the Court of Imperial Rites to oversee sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 初，球言麓川事，振固已銜之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Qiu spoke of Luchuan affairs, Zhen had already harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: From the outset, Wang Zhen had already resented Qiu for his comments on the Luchuan campaign.

sentences.zh: 欽天監正彭德清者，球鄉人也，素為振腹心。

translations.literal: Peng Deqing, Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, was a fellow townsman of Qiu's and had long been Zhen's trusted confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Deqing, Director of the Directorate of Astronomy, was Qiu's fellow townsman and had long been Wang Zhen's intimate ally.

sentences.zh: 凡天文有變，皆匿不奏，倚振勢為奸，公卿多趨謁。

translations.literal: Whenever there were celestial anomalies, he concealed them and did not report them; relying on Zhen's power he committed wrongdoing, and many ministers and grandees hurried to pay court to him.
translations.idiomatic: He habitually concealed astronomical portents instead of reporting them, used Wang Zhen's influence for corrupt ends, and senior officials flocked to pay him court.

sentences.zh: 球絕不與通。

translations.literal: Qiu absolutely would not associate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu steadfastly refused any contact with him.

sentences.zh: 德清恨之，遂摘疏中攬權語，謂振曰：「此指公耳。」

translations.literal: Deqing hated him for this, and thereupon picked out from the memorial language about grasping power, saying to Zhen: "This points at Your Excellency.
translations.idiomatic: Deqing nursed a grudge and plucked from the memorial its passages about usurped authority, telling Wang Zhen: "He is referring to you."

sentences.zh: 振益大怒。

translations.literal: Zhen became still more enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen's rage only grew.

sentences.zh: 會璘疏上，振遂指球同謀，並逮下詔獄，屬指揮馬順殺球。

translations.literal: When Lin's memorial came up, Zhen thereupon pointed to Qiu as co-conspirator; both were seized and sent to the imperial prison; he entrusted the killing of Qiu to Commander Ma Shun.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Lin's petition arrived, Wang Zhen accused Qiu of conspiracy, had both men imprisoned in the imperial jail, and ordered Commander Ma Shun to kill Qiu.

sentences.zh: 順深夜攜一小校持刀至球所。

translations.literal: Shun, deep in the night, brought a junior officer bearing a knife to Qiu's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shun went to Qiu's cell deep in the night, accompanied by a junior guard carrying a knife.

sentences.zh: 球方臥，起立，大呼太祖、太宗。

translations.literal: Qiu was just lying down; he rose and cried out loudly "Taizu, Taizong!"
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had been lying down; he sprang up and cried out the names of Taizu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 頸斷，體猶植。

translations.literal: His neck was severed, yet his body still stood upright.
translations.idiomatic: His neck was cut through, yet his body remained standing.

sentences.zh: 遂支解之，瘞獄戶下。

translations.literal: They thereupon dismembered him and buried him beneath the prison door.
translations.idiomatic: They then dismembered the corpse and buried the pieces beneath the prison gate.

sentences.zh: 璘從旁竊血裙遺球家。

translations.literal: Lin, from the side, secretly took a blood-stained skirt and sent it to Qiu's family.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Lin stole a blood-soaked garment from the scene and sent it to Qiu's family.

sentences.zh: 後其子鉞求得一臂，裹裙以殮。

translations.literal: Later his son Yue obtained one arm and wrapped it in the skirt for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son Yue recovered one arm and wrapped it in the bloodied garment for burial.

sentences.zh: 順有子病久，忽起捽順發，拳且蹴之曰：「老賊，令爾他日禍逾我！

translations.literal: Shun had a son who had been ill long; suddenly he rose, seized Shun by the hair, and with fists and kicks said: "Old villain, may your calamity in days to come exceed mine!
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shun's son, who had been gravely ill for a long time, suddenly sat up, seized his father by the hair, and beat and kicked him, crying: "You old villain—in days to come may your suffering surpass mine!

sentences.zh: 我，劉球也。」

translations.literal: I—Liu Qiu."
translations.idiomatic: I am Liu Qiu."

sentences.zh: 順驚悸。

translations.literal: Shun was startled and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shun was terrified.

sentences.zh: 俄而子死，小校亦死。

translations.literal: Before long the son died, and the junior officer also died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the son died, and the junior guard died as well.

sentences.zh: 璘，字德文，高郵人。

translations.literal: Lin, style name Dewen, was a native of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Lin, styled Dewen, was a native of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 有孝行。

translations.literal: He had filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 獄解，遂歸，不復出。

translations.literal: When the prison case was cleared, he returned home and never came forth again.
translations.idiomatic: After he was released from prison, he returned home and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 球死數年，瓦剌果入寇。

translations.literal: Several years after Qiu's death, the Oirats indeed raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: A few years after Liu Qiu's death, the Oirats invaded as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，振被殺。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong was taken north on campaign; Zhen was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong was captured on the northern campaign, and Wang Zhen was killed.

sentences.zh: 朝士立擊順，斃之。

translations.literal: Court officials immediately struck Shun down and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials fell upon Ma Shun on the spot and beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 而德清自土木遁還，下獄論斬，尋瘐死。

translations.literal: Deqing, having fled back from Tumu, was sent to prison and sentenced to decapitation; soon he died of illness in custody.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Deqing, who had escaped back from the Tumu disaster, was imprisoned, sentenced to death, and soon died of illness in jail.

sentences.zh: 詔戮其屍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his corpse dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued ordering his corpse to be mutilated in posthumous punishment.

sentences.zh: 景帝憐球忠，贈翰林學士，謚忠湣，立祠於鄉。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing pitied Qiu's loyalty, posthumously granted him Grand Secretary of the Hanlin Academy, gave the posthumous name Zhongmin, and erected a shrine in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, moved by Qiu's loyalty, posthumously made him a Hanlin Academician, conferred the posthumous name Loyal and Lamented, and built a memorial shrine in his hometown.

sentences.zh: 球二子，長鉞、次釪。

translations.literal: Qiu had two sons: the elder Yue, the younger Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu had two sons—the elder Yue and the younger Yu.

sentences.zh: 皆篤學，躬耕養母。
