translations.literal: Both were devoted to learning and personally tilled fields to support their mother.
translations.idiomatic: Both were devoted scholars who farmed with their own hands to support their mother.

sentences.zh: 球既得恤，兄弟乃出應舉，先後成進士。

translations.literal: After Qiu received posthumous honors, the brothers then came forth to take the examinations and in succession became metropolitan graduates.
translations.idiomatic: Once their father had been honored posthumously, the brothers entered the examinations and both passed the metropolitan degree in turn.

sentences.zh: 鉞，廣東參政；

translations.literal: Yue was Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong;
translations.idiomatic: Yue served as Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong;

sentences.zh: 釪，雲南按察使。

translations.literal: Yu was Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu served as Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 陳鑒，字貞明，高安人。

translations.literal: Chen Jian, style name Zhenming, was a native of Gao'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jian, styled Zhenming, was a native of Gao'an.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Messenger.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a palace messenger.

sentences.zh: 正統中，擢御史。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong period he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 出按順天。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to inspect the Shuntian circuit.

sentences.zh: 言京師風俗澆漓，其故有五：一，事佛過甚；

translations.literal: He said the customs of the capital are diluted and degraded; the reasons are five: first, excessive devotion to Buddhism;
translations.idiomatic: He reported that morals in the capital had fallen into decay for five reasons: first, excessive Buddhist worship;

sentences.zh: 二，營喪破家；

translations.literal: second, arranging funerals that ruin families;
translations.idiomatic: second, ruinous funeral expenditures;

sentences.zh: 三，服食靡麗；

translations.literal: third, food and dress excessively luxurious;
translations.idiomatic: third, extravagant food and clothing;

sentences.zh: 四，優倡為蠹；

translations.literal: fourth, actors and singers become pests;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, actors and entertainers preying on society;

sentences.zh: 五，博塞成風。

translations.literal: fifth, gambling and dice become the prevailing wind.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, widespread gambling.

sentences.zh: 章下禮部，格不行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites; it was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Rites but was rejected and never enforced.

sentences.zh: 改按貴州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to inspect Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to inspect Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 時麓川酋思任發子思機發遁孟養，屢上書求宥罪通貢。

translations.literal: At that time Si Jifa, son of the Luchuan chieftain Si Renfa, had fled to Mengyang and repeatedly sent memorials begging forgiveness and permission to submit tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Si Jifa, son of the Luchuan chieftain Si Renfa, had fled to Mengyang and repeatedly petitioned for pardon and the right to resume tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 復大舉遠征，兵連不解。

translations.literal: A great distant expedition was again launched; warfare continued without relief.
translations.idiomatic: Instead the court launched another major distant campaign, and fighting dragged on without end.

sentences.zh: 雲、貴軍民疲敝。

translations.literal: The armies and people of Yunnan and Guizhou were worn out and impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians in Yunnan and Guizhou were exhausted and destitute.

sentences.zh: 苗乘機煽動，閩、浙間盜賊大起。

translations.literal: The Miao seized the opportunity to stir unrest; bandits rose greatly in Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao took advantage of the unrest to incite rebellion, and banditry erupted across Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 舉朝皆知其不可，懲劉球禍，無敢諫者。

translations.literal: The whole court knew it could not be done, but fearing Liu Qiu's fate, none dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: The entire court knew the campaign was folly, but mindful of Liu Qiu's fate, no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，鑒抗疏言賊酋遠遁，不為邊患，宜專責雲南守臣相機剿滅，無遠勞禁旅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year Jian memorialized in opposition, saying the bandit chieftain had fled far away and was no border threat; Yunnan frontier officials alone should be charged to destroy him according to circumstances, without far tiring the capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year Chen Jian submitted a bold memorial arguing that the rebel chief had fled beyond reach and posed no border threat—that Yunnan's frontier commanders should be entrusted to eliminate him as circumstances allowed, without sending the capital army on a distant campaign.

sentences.zh: 王振怒，欲困之，改鑒雲南參議，使赴騰沖招賊。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen was enraged and wished to trap him; Jian was transferred to Assistant Administrative Commissioner of Yunnan and sent to Tengchong to recruit the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen was furious and sought to ruin him, reassigning Chen Jian as Assistant Administrative Commissioner of Yunnan and dispatching him to Tengchong to negotiate with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 已，復摭鑒為巡按時嘗請改四川播州宣慰司隸貴州，為鑒罪，令兵部劾之，論死系獄。

translations.literal: Before long, he again picked out that when Jian was touring inspector he had once requested to transfer Sichuan's Bozhou Pacification Commission to Guizhou jurisdiction as Jian's offense; the Ministry of War was ordered to impeach him; he was sentenced to death and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Zhen dredged up an old proposal Chen Jian had made as touring censor to transfer Sichuan's Bozhou Pacification Commission to Guizhou's jurisdiction, used it as grounds for prosecution, had the Ministry of War impeach him, and had him sentenced to death and thrown in prison.

sentences.zh: 景帝嗣位，乃得赦。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing succeeded to the throne, he was then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Emperor Jing took the throne was he granted amnesty.

sentences.zh: 尋授河南參議。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Assistant Administrative Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Assistant Administrative Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 致仕歸，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to private life and died at home.

sentences.zh: 自正統中，劉球以忤王振冤死，鑒繼下獄，中外莫敢言事者數年。

translations.literal: From the Zhengtong period, Liu Qiu died unjustly for opposing Wang Zhen; Jian afterward also entered prison—for several years throughout court and country none dared speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhengtong period onward, after Liu Qiu was wrongfully killed for opposing Wang Zhen and Chen Jian was imprisoned in turn, for years no one inside or outside the court dared raise policy matters.

sentences.zh: 至景帝時，言路始開，爭發憤上書。

translations.literal: By Emperor Jing's time the avenue of speech was first opened; many indignantly submitted memorials in competition.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jing the channels of remonstrance slowly reopened, and officials vied to vent their outrage in memorials.

sentences.zh: 有何觀者，復以言得罪去。

translations.literal: There was He Guan, who again was dismissed for offending through speech.
translations.idiomatic: He Guan was among them, and he too was punished and removed for speaking out.

sentences.zh: 觀以善書為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Guan, on account of excellent calligraphy, [served] as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was appointed Secretariat Drafter for his skill in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年劾尚書王直輩正統時阿附權奸，不宜在左右。

translations.literal: In Jingtai year 2 he impeached Minister Wang Zhi and his like for toadying to the powerful villain during the Zhengtong era, [saying they] were unfit to remain at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingtai he impeached Minister Wang Zhi and others for having fawned on the powerful villain Wang Zhen during the Zhengtong reign, declaring them unfit to remain at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 中貴見「權奸」語，以為侵已，激帝怒，下科道參議。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs saw the words "powerful villain," took them as an attack on themselves, inflamed the emperor's anger, and had the censorate and surveillance officials debate [the case].
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs took the phrase "powerful villain" as a personal attack, whipped up the emperor's wrath, and had the censorial and surveillance officials review the matter.

sentences.zh: 吏科毛玉主奏稿，力詆觀，林聰、葉盛持之，乃刪削奏上。

translations.literal: Mao Yu of the Department of Personnel led the drafting of the memorial, vigorously denouncing Guan; Lin Cong and Ye Sheng resisted, and [the text] was then trimmed before submission.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yu of the Department of Personnel drafted the memorial and fiercely attacked Guan, but Lin Cong and Ye Sheng intervened, and the document was finally edited down before it was submitted.

sentences.zh: 會御史疏亦上，中有「觀考滿不遷，私憾吏部」語。

translations.literal: Just then a supervising censor's memorial also went up, containing the words "Guan completed his term of review without promotion and bears a private grudge against the Ministry of Personnel."
translations.idiomatic: At the same time a supervising censor submitted a memorial containing the words "Guan had failed to receive promotion after completing his term of review and nursed a private grudge against the Ministry of Personnel."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下觀詔獄，杖之，謫九溪衛經歷。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, sent Guan down to the imperial prison, beat him with the rod, and banished him to be Administrator of Jiuxi Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, had Guan sent to the imperial prison, beaten with the rod, and demoted to Administrator of Jiuxi Guard.

sentences.zh: 鐘同，字世京，吉安永豐人。

translations.literal: Zhong Tong, styled Shijing, was a man of Yongfeng in Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Tong, styled Shijing, was a native of Yongfeng in Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 父復，宣德中進士及第。

translations.literal: His father Fu passed the jinshi examinations and took highest honors in the Xuande era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu passed the jinshi examinations with highest honors during the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官修撰，與劉球善。

translations.literal: Having served in office as Compiler, he was on good terms with Liu Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Compiler and was close friends with Liu Qiu.

sentences.zh: 球上封事，約與俱，復妻勸止之。

translations.literal: Qiu submitted a sealed memorial and arranged to go together [with him]; Fu's wife urged that he stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu submitted a sealed memorial and asked Fu to join him, Fu's wife urged her husband not to go.

sentences.zh: 球詣復邸，邀偕行。

translations.literal: Qiu went to Fu's residence and invited [him] to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu went to Fu's house and asked him to come along.

sentences.zh: 復已他往，妻從屏間詈曰：「汝自上疏，何累他人為！」

translations.literal: Fu had already gone elsewhere; his wife cursed from behind the screen, saying: "You submit your own memorial—why drag others into it!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu had already left for elsewhere. From behind the screen his wife shouted curses: "You want to submit your own memorial—why drag other people into it!"

sentences.zh: 球出嘆曰：「彼乃謀及婦人。」

translations.literal: Qiu went out and sighed, saying: "He even lets his wife into his plotting."
translations.idiomatic: Qiu left and sighed: "He even consults his wife when making plans."

sentences.zh: 遂獨上奏，竟死。

translations.literal: Then he went up alone with his memorial and in the end died [for it].
translations.idiomatic: He went on alone to submit his memorial and was eventually put to death.

sentences.zh: 居無何，復亦病死。

translations.literal: Before long, Fu also died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward, Fu too died of illness.

sentences.zh: 妻深悔之，每哭輒曰：「早知爾，曷若與劉君偕死。」

translations.literal: His wife deeply regretted it; each time she wept she would say: "Had I known it would end like this for you, how much better to have died together with Master Liu."
translations.idiomatic: His wife was filled with remorse, and whenever she wept she would say: "If I had known how this would end, I would rather have died together with Master Liu."

sentences.zh: 同幼聞母言，即感奮，思成父誌。

translations.literal: When Tong was young and heard his mother's words, he was immediately stirred and resolved to fulfill his father's unfulfilled purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Tong heard these words from his mother as a boy, and they stirred him at once; he resolved to finish what his father had left undone.

sentences.zh: 嘗入吉安忠節祠，見所祀歐陽修、楊邦乂諸人，嘆曰：「死不入此，非夫也。」

translations.literal: Once he entered the Loyalty and Integrity Shrine in Ji'an, saw those enshrined there—Ouyang Xiu, Yang Bangyi, and the like—and sighed, saying: "To die and not be admitted here is not the act of a true man."
translations.idiomatic: Once he visited the Loyalty and Integrity Shrine in Ji'an and saw the honored names of Ouyang Xiu, Yang Bangyi, and others, he sighed and said: "If I cannot enter this shrine after death, I am no true man."

sentences.zh: 景泰二年舉進士，明年授御史。

translations.literal: In Jingtai year 2 he passed the jinshi examination; the next year he was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the second year of Jingtai and was appointed Supervising Censor the following year.

sentences.zh: 懷獻太子既薨，中外望復沂王於東宮。

translations.literal: After Crown Prince Huai Xian had died, within and without [the court] hoped to restore the Prince of Yi to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the death of Crown Prince Huai Xian, officials inside and outside the court hoped the Prince of Yi would be reinstated as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 同與郎中章綸早朝，語及沂王，皆泣下，因與約疏請復儲。

translations.literal: Tong and Bureau Director Zhang Lun met at the early levee, spoke of the Prince of Yi, and both wept; they then agreed to submit a memorial requesting restoration of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: At the morning audience Tong and Bureau Director Zhang Lun spoke of the Prince of Yi, and both broke into tears. They then agreed to submit a memorial asking that the heir be restored.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，同因上疏論時政，遂及復儲事，其略曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year 5, Tong thereupon submitted a memorial discussing current affairs and then touched on restoring the heir; its gist read:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year Tong submitted a memorial on current affairs that went on to address restoration of the heir. Its gist was as follows:

sentences.zh: 近得賊諜，言也先使偵京師及臨清虛實，期初秋大舉深入，直下河南。

translations.literal: Recently we obtained an enemy spy who said Esen had sent men to reconnoiter the actual strength of the capital and Linqing, planning in early autumn to launch a major advance deep [into the realm], driving straight down into Henan.
translations.idiomatic: We recently captured an enemy spy who reported that Esen had sent scouts to probe the defenses of the capital and Linqing, intending a major invasion in early autumn that would strike deep into the realm and push straight into Henan.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之不勝寒心，而廟堂大臣皆恬不介意。

translations.literal: Your servant, on hearing this, could not overcome a chill in the heart, yet the great ministers in the hall of governance are all placid and take no notice.
translations.idiomatic: I shuddered when I heard this, yet the great ministers at court remain placid and unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 昔秦伐趙，諸侯自若，孔子順獨憂之，人皆以為狂。

translations.literal: Formerly when Qin attacked Zhao, the feudal lords were as if nothing were amiss; Kong Shun alone was troubled—people all thought him mad.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Qin attacked Zhao, the feudal lords acted as if nothing were amiss; only Kong Shun was troubled by it, and everyone thought him mad.

sentences.zh: 臣今者之言，何以異此。

translations.literal: Your servant's words today—how do they differ from this?
translations.idiomatic: How are my words today any different?

sentences.zh: 臣草茅時，聞寺人構惡，戕戮直臣劉球，遂致廷臣箝口。

translations.literal: When your servant was still in obscurity, he heard that the eunuchs wove evil plots, slaughtered the upright minister Liu Qiu, and thereby caused court officials to seal their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Before I entered office I heard how eunuchs had plotted evil, cut down the upright minister Liu Qiu, and thereby silenced the entire court.

sentences.zh: 假使當時犯顏有人，必能諫止上皇之行，何至有蒙塵之禍。

translations.literal: Had there then been someone who dared face wrath and remonstrate, he would surely have been able to admonish and stop the Former Emperor's expedition—how would we have reached the calamity of the imperial carriage besmirched [in captivity]?
translations.idiomatic: If someone had then had the courage to speak bluntly to the throne, he could surely have stopped the Former Emperor's campaign—how then could the calamity of imperial capture have befallen us?

sentences.zh: 陛下赫然中興，鋤奸黨，旌忠直。

translations.literal: Your Majesty arose brilliantly and restored the dynasty, uprooted villainous factions, and honored the loyal and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has brilliantly restored the dynasty, uprooted villainous factions, and honored loyal and upright men.

sentences.zh: 命六師禦敵於郊，不戰而三軍之氣自倍。

translations.literal: You ordered the Six Armies to resist the enemy beyond the capital; without fighting, the morale of the three armies itself doubled.
translations.idiomatic: You sent the armies to meet the enemy beyond the walls; even without battle the spirit of the troops doubled on its own.

sentences.zh: 臣謂陛下方且鞭撻四裔，坐致太平，奈何邊氛甫息，瘡痍未復，而侈心遽生，失天下望。

translations.literal: Your servant thought Your Majesty was just then about to lash the four frontier peoples and bring peace while seated—yet why, when border troubles have barely subsided and wounds are not yet healed, does extravagant desire suddenly arise and lose the hope of all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: I believed Your Majesty was on the verge of subduing the barbarians on every side and securing peace at a stroke. Yet the border is barely quiet, the wounds of the realm are scarcely healed, and already a taste for extravagance has sprung up, forfeiting the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: 伏願取鑒前車，厚自奮厲。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I wish Your Majesty would take the overturned cart ahead as a mirror and vigorously steel yourself.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to learn from past mistakes and redouble your resolve.

sentences.zh: 毋徇貨色，毋甘嬉遊。

translations.literal: Do not indulge goods and women; do not content yourself with frivolous roaming.
translations.idiomatic: Do not indulge in wealth and pleasure; do not surrender yourself to idle amusements.

sentences.zh: 親庶政以總威權，敦倫理以厚風俗，辨邪正以專委任，嚴賞罰以彰善惡，崇風憲以正紀綱。

translations.literal: Attend personally to the multitude of state affairs to gather authority in your hands; cultivate human relations to thicken custom; distinguish the crooked from the straight to concentrate appointments; be strict in rewards and punishments to display good and evil; exalt inspection and law to rectify discipline and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Attend personally to the business of government and hold authority firmly in your own hands; nurture the bonds of family and society to strengthen public morals; distinguish loyal from treacherous men and entrust office accordingly; enforce rewards and punishments strictly so that good and evil are plain; uphold law and discipline to restore order throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 去浮費，罷冗員。

translations.literal: Remove frivolous expenditures; abolish redundant posts.
translations.idiomatic: Cut wasteful spending and eliminate superfluous offices.

sentences.zh: 禁僧道之蠹民，擇賢將以訓士。

translations.literal: Prohibit monks and Daoists from being parasites on the people; select worthy generals to train troops.
translations.idiomatic: Restrain the monks and Daoists who prey upon the people; choose able commanders to train the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 然後親率群臣，謝過郊廟，如成湯之六事自責，唐太宗之十漸即改，庶幾天意可回，國勢可振。

translations.literal: Then lead the myriad ministers in person, confess faults at the suburban altars—as Cheng Tang blamed himself for six matters, as Tang Taizong immediately corrected the ten gradual [faults]—so that perhaps Heaven's intent may be turned back and the nation's strength may be revived.
translations.idiomatic: Then lead the court in person to confess your faults before Heaven and the ancestral altars—as Cheng Tang blamed himself for six offenses, as Tang Taizong promptly corrected his ten gradual faults—so that Heaven's favor may be restored and the nation's strength renewed.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He further said:
translations.idiomatic: He went on to say:

sentences.zh: 父有天下，固當傳之於子。

translations.literal: A father who holds all under Heaven ought naturally to pass it to his son.
translations.idiomatic: When a father possesses the realm, he should naturally pass it to his son.

sentences.zh: 乃者太子薨逝，足知天命有在。

translations.literal: Recently the crown prince died and departed—this is enough to show that Heaven's mandate has its due place.
translations.idiomatic: The recent death of the crown prince is proof enough that Heaven's mandate rests elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為上皇之子，即陛下之子。

translations.literal: Your servant privately holds that the Former Emperor's son is precisely Your Majesty's son.
translations.idiomatic: I privately hold that the Former Emperor's son is Your Majesty's own son as well.

sentences.zh: 沂王天資厚重，足令宗社有托。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi is by nature steady and substantial, sufficient to let the ancestral altars and the state have one to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yi is by nature steady and dependable—surely fit to bear the weight of the realm.

sentences.zh: 伏望擴天地之量，敦友於之仁，蠲吉具儀，建復儲位，實祖宗無疆之休。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I hope Your Majesty will expand the measure of Heaven and Earth, thicken the benevolence of brotherly harmony, choose an auspicious day and complete the rites, establish and restore the position of heir—truly unending felicity for the ancestral sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to broaden your generosity as Heaven and Earth are broad, deepen the kindness owed between brothers, choose an auspicious day and complete the rites, and restore the heir apparent—this would be boundless blessing for the ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He further said:
translations.idiomatic: He added further:

sentences.zh: 陛下命將帥各陳方略。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ordered generals and commanders each to set forth strategic plans.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ordered your generals and commanders each to submit strategic plans.

sentences.zh: 經旬逾時，互相委責。

translations.literal: Weeks passed beyond the deadline, and they shifted blame onto one another.
translations.idiomatic: Weeks went by past the deadline while they merely blamed one another.

sentences.zh: 及石亨、柳溥有言，又不過庸人孺子之計。

translations.literal: When Shi Heng and Liu Pu did speak, it was nothing beyond the plans of mediocre men and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Heng and Liu Pu finally spoke, their proposals were no better than the schemes of mediocrities and children.

sentences.zh: 平時尚爾，一旦有急，將何策制之？

translations.literal: In ordinary times it is still thus—once urgency arises, with what plan will you control it?
translations.idiomatic: If this is how they behave in peacetime, what strategy will avail you in a crisis?

sentences.zh: 夫禦敵之方，莫先用賢。

translations.literal: As for the method of resisting the enemy, nothing comes before first employing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In resisting the enemy, there is no priority higher than employing worthy men.

sentences.zh: 陛下求賢若渴，而大臣之排抑尤甚，所舉者率多親舊富厚之家。

translations.literal: Your Majesty seeks the worthy as if thirsty, yet the great ministers' suppression is especially severe; those recommended are for the most part from kin, old friends, and wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty thirsts for worthy men, yet your chief ministers suppress talent all the more ruthlessly; most of those they recommend come from among their kin, old friends, and the rich.

sentences.zh: 即長材屈抑，孰肯為言？

translations.literal: Even when men of outstanding talent are held down, who is willing to speak for them?
translations.idiomatic: When men of exceptional talent are kept down, who will speak up for them?

sentences.zh: 朝臣欺謾若此，臣所以撫膺流涕，為今日妨賢病國者醜也。

translations.literal: Court ministers deceive and evade thus—this is why your servant beats his breast and weeps tears, ashamed of those who today obstruct the worthy and sicken the state.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers deceive the throne like this—this is why I beat my breast and weep with shame at those who today obstruct talent and poison the state.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝不懌。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 下廷臣集議。

translations.literal: He sent it down for the court ministers to assemble and deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the court ministers to assemble and discuss it.

sentences.zh: 寧陽侯陳懋、吏部尚書王直等請帝納其言，因引罪求罷。

translations.literal: Marquis Chen Mao of Ningyang, Minister Wang Zhi of the Ministry of Personnel, and others asked the emperor to accept his words and, citing guilt, requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Chen Mao of Ningyang, Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi, and others urged the emperor to heed the memorial and, taking blame upon themselves, asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted them and kept them in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted them and kept them at their posts.

sentences.zh: 越數日，章綸亦疏言復儲事，遂並下詔獄。

translations.literal: After several days Zhang Lun also submitted a memorial on restoring the heir, and they were thereupon both sent down to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Zhang Lun too memorialized on restoring the heir, and both men were sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，大理少卿廖莊亦以言沂王事予杖。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year Vice Minister of Justice Liao Zhuang also received beatings for speaking on the matter of the Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the following year Vice Minister of Justice Liao Zhuang was also beaten for speaking on behalf of the Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 左右言：事由同倡，帝乃封巨梃就獄中杖之，同竟死。

translations.literal: Those at the emperor's side said the matter originated with Tong's advocacy; the emperor thereupon sealed a great rod, went to the prison to beat him, and Tong in the end died.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers said the affair had been Tong's doing; the emperor then had a heavy club sealed, went to the prison to beat him, and Tong died.

sentences.zh: 時年三十二。

translations.literal: He was then thirty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-two years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 同之上疏也，策馬出，馬伏地不肯起。

translations.literal: When Tong was going up with his memorial, he spurred his horse to go out; the horse crouched on the ground and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong set out to submit his memorial, he mounted his horse to ride off, but the horse dropped to the ground and refused to rise.

sentences.zh: 同叱曰：「吾不畏死，爾奚為者！」

translations.literal: Tong rebuked [it], saying: "I do not fear death—what are you doing!"
translations.idiomatic: Tong shouted at it: "I am not afraid to die—what are you afraid of!"

sentences.zh: 馬猶盤辟再四，乃行。

translations.literal: The horse still circled and wove back and forth again and again, and only then went.
translations.idiomatic: The horse still pranced and circled again and again before it would go.

sentences.zh: 同死，馬長號數聲亦死。

translations.literal: When Tong died, the horse wailed loudly several times and also died.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong died, the horse gave several long cries and died as well.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，贈同大理左寺丞，錄其子啟為國子生，尋授咸寧知縣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ying returned to the throne, Tong was posthumously granted Left Assistant Director in the Court of the Judiciary, and his son Qi was enrolled as a student of the Imperial Academy; soon after he was appointed Magistrate of Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ying regained the throne, Tong was posthumously honored as Left Assistant Director in the Court of the Judiciary; his son Qi was enrolled in the Imperial Academy and soon appointed magistrate of Xianning.

sentences.zh: 啟請父遺骸歸葬，詔給舟車路費。

translations.literal: Qi requested his father's remains for burial at home, and an edict granted boat, carriage, and travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Qi asked to bring his father's remains home for burial, and the court granted funds for boat, carriage, and travel.

sentences.zh: 成化中，授次子越通政知事，給同妻羅氏月廩。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua era his second son Yue was appointed Secretary in the Office of Transmission, and Tong's wife Lady Luo was given a monthly grain allowance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign his second son Yue was appointed Secretary in the Office of Transmission, and Tong's wife Lady Luo received a monthly grain stipend.

sentences.zh: 尋賜同謚恭湣，從祀忠節祠，與球聯位，竟如同初誌。

translations.literal: Soon Tong was granted the posthumous title Gong Min, given accompanying sacrifice at the Loyalty and Integrity Shrine, paired in place with Qiu—in the end just as Tong's original aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was soon granted the posthumous name Gong Min and given a place in the Loyalty and Integrity Shrine beside Qiu, fulfilling the ambition he had held from the first.

sentences.zh: 方同下獄時，有禮部郎孟玘者，亦疏言復儲事。

translations.literal: Just as Tong was sent down to prison, there was Secretariat Director Meng Qi of the Ministry of Rites, who also submitted a memorial on restoring the heir.
translations.idiomatic: While Tong was in prison, Meng Qi, a director in the Ministry of Rites, also memorialized on restoring the heir.

sentences.zh: 帝不罪。

translations.literal: The emperor did not punish [him].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 而進士楊集上書于謙曰：「奸人黃矰獻議易儲，不過為逃死計耳，公等遽成之。

translations.literal: But jinshi Yang Ji wrote to Yu Qian, saying: "The villain Huang Zeng offered the plan to change the heir—it was nothing but a scheme to escape death, and you gentlemen hastily carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: But the newly minted jinshi Yang Ji wrote to Yu Qian: "The villain Huang Zeng proposed changing the heir merely to save his own skin, and you gentlemen rushed to execute the plan.

sentences.zh: 公國家柱石，獨不思所以善後乎？

translations.literal: You are the state's pillar—do you alone not think how to handle the aftermath?
translations.idiomatic: You are the pillar of the state—do you not consider how to settle matters afterward?

sentences.zh: 今同等又下獄矣，脫諸人死杖下，而公等坐享崇高，如清議何！」

translations.literal: Now Tong and his like are again sent down to prison. If these men die under the rod while you gentlemen sit enjoying lofty rank—what of pure public opinion!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Tong and the rest are imprisoned again. If they die under the rod while you sit in exalted office—what will become of public trust in your integrity!"

sentences.zh: 謙以書示王文。

translations.literal: Qian took the letter and showed it to Wang Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Qian showed the letter to Wang Wen.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「書生不知忌諱，要為有膽，當進一官處之。」

translations.literal: Wen said: "The lettered man knows no taboo—after all he has courage; he ought to be promoted one rank and given a post."
translations.idiomatic: Wen said: "This student knows no restraint, but at least he has courage. Give him a promotion and an appointment."

sentences.zh: 乃以集知安州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ji was made Magistrate of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was thereupon appointed magistrate of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 玘，閩人；

translations.literal: Qi was a man of Min;
translations.idiomatic: Qi was a native of Fujian;

sentences.zh: 集，常熟人也。

translations.literal: Ji was a man of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was a native of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 章綸，字大經，樂清人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lun, styled Dajing, was a man of Yueqing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun, styled Dajing, was a native of Yueqing.

sentences.zh: 正統四年進士。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong year 4 he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the fourth year of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 授南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed as Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，召為儀制郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai he was summoned to be Bureau Director of Ritual Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingtai reign he was summoned to serve as Bureau Director of Ritual Regulations.

sentences.zh: 綸見國家多故，每慷慨論事。

translations.literal: Lun saw that the state had many troubles and each time spoke vigorously on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm beset by one crisis after another, Lun spoke out passionately on public affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗上太平十六策，反復萬餘言。

translations.literal: Once he submitted Sixteen Policies for Great Peace, going back and forth for more than ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted his Sixteen Policies for Great Peace—more than ten thousand words in all.

sentences.zh: 也先既議和，請力圖修攘以待其變。

translations.literal: After Esen had already negotiated peace, he requested to strive mightily to cultivate defense and attack while awaiting his changes.
translations.idiomatic: After Esen had agreed to peace, he urged the court to strengthen both defense and offense while watching for a shift in the enemy's fortunes.

sentences.zh: 中官興安請帝建大隆福寺成，將臨幸。

translations.literal: The eunuch Xing An asked the emperor, when the great Longfu Temple was completed, to visit it in person.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Xing An urged the emperor to visit the newly completed Great Longfu Temple in person.

sentences.zh: 綸具疏諫，河東鹽運判官濟南楊浩除官未行，亦上章諫，帝即罷幸。

translations.literal: Lun submitted a detailed memorial to remonstrate; Yang Hao of Jinan, Salt Transport Judge of Hedong, having received appointment but not yet taken up his post, also submitted a chapter to remonstrate—and the emperor immediately abandoned the visit.
translations.idiomatic: Lun submitted a detailed memorial in protest. Yang Hao of Jinan, who had been appointed Salt Transport Judge of Hedong but had not yet taken up his post, also remonstrated, and the emperor at once canceled the visit.

sentences.zh: 浩後累官副都御史，巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: Hao later rose through offices to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Yansui.
translations.idiomatic: Hao later rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief and served as Grand Coordinator of Yansui.

sentences.zh: 綸又因災異請求致變之由，語頗切至。

translations.literal: Lun again, because of calamities and omens, requested the causes that brought the changes; his language was rather incisive and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Lun also memorialized after omens and disasters, asking what had provoked them; his language was blunt and pressing.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，鐘同上奏請復儲。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of year 5 Zhong Tong went up with a memorial requesting restoration of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year Zhong Tong submitted a memorial requesting restoration of the heir.

sentences.zh: 越二日，綸亦抗疏陳修德弭災十四事。

translations.literal: After two days Lun also submitted a forthright memorial setting forth fourteen matters of cultivating virtue and stopping calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Zhang Lun submitted a bold memorial outlining fourteen measures to cultivate virtue and avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 其大者謂：「內官不可幹外政，佞臣不可假事權，後宮不可盛聲色。

translations.literal: Among the greater [points] he said: "Palace eunuchs must not interfere in external governance; flattering ministers must not be lent affairs and power; the rear palace must not overflow with music and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: His chief points were these: "Palace eunuchs must not meddle in civil government; sycophants must not be granted real power; the inner palace must not be overrun with music and women.

sentences.zh: 凡陰盛之屬，請悉禁罷。」

translations.literal: All things belonging to yin in excess—request that they all be prohibited and abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Everything excessive in yin influence should be forbidden and abolished."

sentences.zh: 又言：「孝弟者，百行之本。

translations.literal: He further said: "Filial piety and brotherliness are the root of the hundred conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Filial piety and brotherly duty are the foundation of all proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 願退朝後朝謁兩宮皇太后，修問安視膳之儀。

translations.literal: I wish that after retiring from court Your Majesty would attend audience at the two palaces of the empress dowagers and restore the rites of inquiring after their health and attending their meals.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that after court you visit the two empress dowagers and restore the rites of inquiring after their health and sharing their meals.

sentences.zh: 上皇君臨天下十有四年，是天下之父也；

translations.literal: The Former Emperor ruled all under Heaven for fourteen years—he is the father of all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The Former Emperor ruled the realm for fourteen years—he is father to the whole empire;

sentences.zh: 陛下親受冊封，是上皇之臣也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally received investiture by sealed edict—you are the Former Emperor's minister.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received the throne by formal investiture—you are subject to the Former Emperor.

sentences.zh: 陛下與上皇，雖殊形體，實同一人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty and the Former Emperor, though different in bodily form, are in reality one person.
translations.idiomatic: You and the Former Emperor are two bodies but one man.

sentences.zh: 伏讀奉迎還宮之詔曰：『禮惟加而無替，義以卑而奉尊。』

translations.literal: Prostrate, I have read the edict welcoming [him] back to the palace, which says: 'In ritual there is only increase and no displacement; in righteousness the humble serves the honored.
translations.idiomatic: I have read again the edict that welcomed him back to the palace: 'In ritual rank is added, never set aside; in righteousness the lesser serves the greater.'

sentences.zh: 望陛下允蹈斯言。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will consent to tread upon these words.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to live up to these words.

sentences.zh: 或朔望，或節旦，率群臣朝見延和門，以展友於之情，實天下之至願也。

translations.literal: Whether on the first and fifteenth of the month, or on festival mornings, leading all ministers to attend audience at Yanhe Gate, thereby to display the feeling of friendship between brothers—this is truly the utmost wish of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth of each month, or on festival mornings, lead your ministers in audience at Yanhe Gate to show brotherly affection—that is the dearest wish of the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 更請復汪後於中宮，正天下之母儀；

translations.literal: Further request to restore Empress Wang to the Central Palace and rectify the motherly model for all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: I further ask that Empress Wang be restored to the empress's palace, so that the empire once again has a proper exemplar of motherhood;

sentences.zh: 還沂王之儲位，定天下之大本。

translations.literal: Return the Prince of Yi's position as heir and fix the great foundation of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the Prince of Yi to his status as heir and secure the fundamental order of the realm.

sentences.zh: 如此則和氣充溢，災沴自弭。」

translations.literal: If it is thus, then harmonious qi will fill and overflow, and calamities and pestilence will naturally cease."
translations.idiomatic: Do this, and harmony will flourish while disasters and portents fade away of themselves."

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝大怒。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; the Emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 時日已暝，宮門閉。

translations.literal: At that time the sun had already set, and the palace gates were closed.
translations.idiomatic: Night had fallen and the palace gates were already shut.

sentences.zh: 乃傳旨自門隙中出，立執綸及鐘同下詔獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon an order was transmitted out through a gap in the gate, and immediately Lun and Zhong Tong were seized and sent down to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was passed out through the crack in the gate, and Zhang Lun and Zhong Tong were at once arrested and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 榜掠慘酷，逼引主使及交通南宮狀。

translations.literal: They were beaten and tortured with cruel severity, forced to implicate the chief instigator and the circumstances of communicating with the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under brutal beating and torture they were pressed to confess who had masterminded the plot and how they had been in contact with the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 瀕死，無一語。

translations.literal: On the verge of death, not a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Even at death's door they would not speak a word.

sentences.zh: 會大風揚沙，晝晦，獄得稍緩，令錮之。

translations.literal: It happened that a great wind raised sand; the day was darkened; the prison proceedings were slightly eased, and they were ordered to be imprisoned in irons.
translations.idiomatic: A violent sandstorm darkened the sky at midday; interrogations eased somewhat, and both men were left in shackles.

sentences.zh: 明年杖廖莊闕下。

translations.literal: The next year Liao Zhuang was beaten with rods below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Liao Zhuang was flogged at court beneath the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 因封杖就獄中杖綸、同各百。

translations.literal: Thereupon sealed rods were carried into the prison, and Lun and Tong were each beaten a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Executioners were then dispatched to the prison with sealed rods, and Zhang Lun and Zhong Tong were each given a hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 同竟死，綸長系如故。

translations.literal: Tong in the end died; Lun remained in long-term imprisonment as before.
translations.idiomatic: Tong died from the beating; Zhang Lun remained in prison as before.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，郭登言綸與廖莊、林聰、左鼎、倪敬等皆直言忤時，宜加旌擢。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, Guo Deng said that Lun together with Liao Zhuang, Lin Cong, Zuo Ding, Ni Jing, and others had all spoken forthrightly in defiance of the times and ought to be specially commended and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Guo Deng argued that Zhang Lun, Liao Zhuang, Lin Cong, Zuo Ding, Ni Jing, and others had all spoken unwelcome truths during the reign and deserved special honors and advancement.

sentences.zh: 帝乃立釋綸。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon immediately released Lun.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor at once ordered Zhang Lun freed.

sentences.zh: 命內侍檢前疏，不得。

translations.literal: He ordered palace attendants to search out the earlier memorial but it could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered eunuchs to locate the earlier memorial, but it could not be found.

sentences.zh: 內侍從旁誦數語，帝嗟嘆再三，擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: A palace attendant recited several phrases from the side; the Emperor sighed repeatedly and promoted him to Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch recited a few lines from memory; the Emperor sighed again and again, then promoted him to Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 綸既以大節為帝所重，而性亢直，不能諧俗。

translations.literal: Lun, having already been prized by the Emperor for his great integrity, was by nature lofty and straight and could not harmonize with custom.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Emperor now valued Zhang Lun for his moral courage, he was uncompromising by nature and ill suited to court manners.

sentences.zh: 石亨貴幸招公卿飲，綸辭不往，又數與尚書楊善論事不合。

translations.literal: Shi Heng, favored and fortunate, invited the chief ministers to drink; Lun declined and did not go; moreover he often disputed affairs with Minister Yang Shan without agreement.
translations.idiomatic: The favored minister Shi Heng invited senior officials to a banquet; Zhang Lun refused to attend. He also frequently clashed with the Minister Yang Shan over policy.

sentences.zh: 亨、善共短綸。

translations.literal: Heng and Shan together spoke ill of Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng and Yang Shan joined in slandering Zhang Lun.

sentences.zh: 乃調南京禮部，就改吏部。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites in Nanjing and then changed to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and shortly afterward reassigned to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，有司以遺詔請大婚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, the responsible offices, on the basis of the testamentary edict, requested a grand wedding.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong came to the throne, the relevant offices cited the late emperor's testament and asked permission to hold the grand wedding.

sentences.zh: 綸言：「山陵尚新，元朔未改，百日從吉，心寧自安。

translations.literal: Lun said: "The mountain tomb is still fresh; the new year's first month has not yet changed; to follow auspiciousness at the hundredth day—can the heart be at ease by itself?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun argued: "The imperial tomb is still freshly sealed, the new reign year has scarcely begun, and to cast off mourning after a hundred days—how can the heart rest easy?

sentences.zh: 陛下踐阼之初，當以孝治天下，三綱五常實原於此。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's treading upon the throne, you ought to govern all under Heaven through filial piety; the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues in truth originate from this.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of your reign you should govern the realm through filial piety; the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues take their root in this alone.

sentences.zh: 乞俟來春舉行。」

translations.literal: I beg to wait until next spring to carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ceremony be postponed until next spring."

sentences.zh: 議雖不從，天下咸重其言。

translations.literal: Though the proposal was not followed, all under Heaven alike honored his words.
translations.idiomatic: Though his advice was rejected, people throughout the realm admired his stand.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，兩淮饑，奏救荒四事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua the two Huai regions suffered famine; he memorialized four matters for famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chenghua reign famine struck the two Huai regions, and he submitted four proposals for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were replied to as approved.
translations.idiomatic: All four were approved.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，子玄應以冒籍舉京闈。

translations.literal: In the autumn of year four his son Xuanying was recommended in the metropolitan examination on false registration.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year his son Xuanying passed the metropolitan examination under a fraudulent household registration.

sentences.zh: 給事中朱清、御史楊智等因劾綸，命侍郎葉盛勘之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhu Qing, Censor Yang Zhi, and others thereupon impeached Lun; the Emperor ordered Vice Minister Ye Sheng to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhu Qing, Censor Yang Zhi, and others impeached Zhang Lun, and the Emperor ordered Vice Minister Ye Sheng to investigate.

sentences.zh: 明年，綸及僉都御史高明考察庶官，兩人議不協。

translations.literal: The next year Lun and Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Ming were inspecting ordinary officials; the two men's opinions did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhang Lun and Vice Censor-in-Chief Gao Ming conducted the routine inspection of officials, and the two could not agree.

sentences.zh: 疏既上，綸復獨奏給事中王讓不赴考察，且言明剛愎自用，己言多不見從，乞與明俱罷。

translations.literal: After the memorial had been submitted, Lun again submitted alone that Supervising Secretary Wang Rang did not come to the inspection, and moreover said that Ming was obstinate and wilful, trusting himself; his own words were often not followed—he begged that he and Ming both be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After their joint report went in, Zhang Lun separately memorialized that Supervising Secretary Wang Rang had failed to attend the inspection, and added that Gao Ming was stubborn and self-willed, that his own recommendations were repeatedly ignored, and that he asked to be dismissed along with Gao Ming.

sentences.zh: 章並下盛等。

translations.literal: The memorials were all sent down to Sheng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials were forwarded to Ye Sheng and his colleagues for review.

sentences.zh: 於是讓及下考諸臣連章劾綸。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rang and the various officials graded in the lower category submitted memorials in succession impeaching Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rang and others who had received poor evaluations then submitted a string of memorials attacking Zhang Lun.

sentences.zh: 綸亦屢疏求罷。

translations.literal: Lun also repeatedly submitted memorials requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun too repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 既而盛等勘上玄應實冒籍。

translations.literal: Before long Sheng and the others investigated and reported upward that Xuanying had in fact falsely registered.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Ye Sheng and his team confirmed that Xuanying had indeed obtained his credentials through fraud.

sentences.zh: 帝宥綸，而所奏他事，亦悉不問。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned Lun, and the other matters he had memorialized were also all not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor excused Zhang Lun and ignored the other charges as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復轉禮部。

translations.literal: Before long he was again transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reassigned back to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 溫州知府範奎被論調官。

translations.literal: Fan Kui, prefect of Wenzhou, was criticized and transferred to another post.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kui, prefect of Wenzhou, was denounced in a memorial and reassigned.

sentences.zh: 綸言：「溫州臣鄉郡，奎大得民心。

translations.literal: Lun said: "Wenzhou is my native commandery; Kui has greatly won the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun wrote: "Wenzhou is my home prefecture, and Fan Kui enjoys great popular support.

sentences.zh: 解官之日，士民三萬人哭泣攀轅，留十八日乃得去。

translations.literal: On the day he left office, thirty thousand gentry and commoners wept and clung to his carriage shafts; they detained him eighteen days before he could depart.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office thirty thousand townspeople wept and seized the shafts of his cart, holding him for eighteen days before he could go.

sentences.zh: 請還之以慰民望。」

translations.literal: Request that he be returned to console the people's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be restored to satisfy the people's hopes."

sentences.zh: 章下所司，竟報寢。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible office; in the end it was reported shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices and in the end was ignored.

sentences.zh: 綸性戇，好直言，不為當事者所喜。

translations.literal: Lun was by nature blunt and honest, fond of speaking straight; he was not liked by those in charge of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and outspoken by nature, Zhang Lun won little favor from those in power.

sentences.zh: 為侍郎二十年，不得遷，請老去。

translations.literal: He served as vice minister for twenty years without advancement and requested to retire in old age.
translations.idiomatic: He spent twenty years as a vice minister without promotion before asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 居數年，其妻張氏上其奏稿，且乞恩。

translations.literal: Several years after [his death], his wife Lady Zhang submitted his memorial drafts and also begged for favor.
translations.idiomatic: Years after his death his wife, Lady Zhang, submitted his memorial drafts and asked the court for special recognition.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉嘆，贈南京禮部尚書，謚恭毅，官一子鴻臚典簿。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and sighed; he posthumously granted him Minister of Rites in Nanjing, with the posthumous title Gongyi, and enfeoffed one son as Director of Ceremonies in the Office of the Imperial Procession.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised him warmly, posthumously appointing him Minister of Rites at Nanjing with the posthumous name Gongyi, and granting one son an office as Director in the Office of Imperial Processions.

sentences.zh: 玄應後舉進士，為南京給事中。

translations.literal: Xuanying later passed the jinshi examination and became a Supervising Secretary in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanying later became a jinshi and served as a Supervising Secretary in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 偕同官論陳鉞罪，忤旨停俸。

translations.literal: Together with fellow officials he discussed Chen Yue's crime and, defying the imperial will, had his salary suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Along with his colleagues he denounced Chen Yue; for defying the throne his stipend was halted.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，上治本五事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he submitted five matters for rectifying governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong came to the throne he submitted five proposals for repairing the foundations of government.

sentences.zh: 仕終廣東布政使。

translations.literal: He served to the end as Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 廖莊，字安止，吉水人。

translations.literal: Liao Zhuang, styled Anzhi, was a man of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Zhuang, courtesy name Anzhi, was a native of Jishui.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 八年改庶吉士，與知縣孔友諒等七人歷事六科。

translations.literal: In year eight he was changed to an Academician-in-Waiting and, together with Magistrate Kong Youliang and six others, rotated through service in the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became a Hanlin bachelor and, with Magistrate Kong Youliang and six others, served rotations in the Six Supervisory Offices.

sentences.zh: 英宗初，授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Yingzong's reign he was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office Scrutinizing Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Yingzong's reign he was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Punishments.

sentences.zh: 正統二年，御史元亮請如詔書蠲邊軍侵沒糧餉，不允。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengtong Censor Yuan Liang requested according to the edict to remit border troops' embezzled grain rations; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhengtong reign Censor Yuan Liang asked that embezzled grain rations owed by border troops be forgiven as the edict promised; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 按察使龔鐩亦請如詔書宥盜犯之未獲者，法司亦寢不行。

translations.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Gong Sui also requested according to the edict to pardon thieves not yet apprehended; the judicial offices likewise shelved it and did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Gong Sui likewise asked that uncaught thieves be amnestied as the edict provided; the judicial offices also let the matter die.

sentences.zh: 莊以詔書當信，上章爭之。

translations.literal: Zhuang, holding that edicts ought to be trusted, submitted a memorial disputing this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang argued that imperial edicts must be honored and memorialized the throne to insist on it.

sentences.zh: 五年詔京官出修荒政，兼征民逋。

translations.literal: In year five an edict ordered capital officials to go out to manage famine relief and concurrently collect overdue taxes from the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict sent capital officials to oversee famine relief while also collecting tax arrears from the populace.

sentences.zh: 莊慮使者督趣困民，請寬災傷州縣，俟秋成。

translations.literal: Zhuang feared the envoys' urgings would distress the people and requested leniency for disaster-stricken prefectures and counties, waiting until the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang worried that the commissioners' pressure would crush the people and asked that disaster-hit counties be given grace until the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 振荒陜西，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Relieving famine in Shaanxi, he preserved and kept alive very many.
translations.idiomatic: While administering famine relief in Shaanxi he saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 還奏寬恤九事，多議行。

translations.literal: On returning he memorialized nine matters of leniency and relief; many were debated and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he submitted nine proposals for lenient relief; most were adopted.

sentences.zh: 楊士奇家人犯法，偕同官論列。

translations.literal: When Yang Shixi's family members violated the law, together with fellow officials he enumerated and criticized the case.
translations.idiomatic: When members of Yang Shixi's household broke the law, he joined fellow officials in denouncing them publicly.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「獨不為楊公地乎？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Do you alone not leave room for Lord Yang?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "Don't you want to give Lord Yang some face?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「正所以為楊公也。」

translations.literal: He said: "It is precisely in order to leave room for Lord Yang."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "This is exactly how I show respect for Lord Yang."

sentences.zh: 八年命與御史張驥同署大理寺事。

translations.literal: In year eight he was ordered together with Censor Zhang Ji to jointly manage the affairs of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was assigned together with Censor Zhang Ji to administer the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 逾月，授左寺丞。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was appointed Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十一年遷南京大理少卿。

translations.literal: In year eleven he was transferred to Vice President of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Vice President of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 逾二年，奸人陳夫者，與所親賈福爭襲指揮職。

translations.literal: After more than two years, a wicked man named Chen Fu and his intimate Jia Fu disputed succession to a commander's post.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later a schemer named Chen Fu and his kinsman Jia Fu fought over who should inherit a military commander's commission.

sentences.zh: 南京刑部侍郎齊韶納夫賄，欲奪福官與之，為莊所駁。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Punishments in Nanjing Qi Shao accepted Fu's bribe and wished to seize Jia Fu's office and give it to him; this was rejected by Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shao, Vice Minister of Punishments in Nanjing, took bribes from Chen Fu and tried to strip Jia Fu of his commission and give it to Chen; Zhuang blocked the scheme.

sentences.zh: 韶捶福至死，被逮。

translations.literal: Shao beat Fu to death and was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shao beat Jia Fu to death and was arrested.

sentences.zh: 夫亦誣莊，俱征下詔獄。

translations.literal: Fu also falsely accused Zhuang; both were summoned down to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fu also framed Zhuang, and both men were hauled before the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 會韶他罪並發，棄市，莊乃得釋。

translations.literal: It happened that Shao's other crimes broke out together; he was executed in the marketplace; Zhuang then obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Shao's other crimes came to light as well he was executed in public, and Zhuang was finally released.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年七月上疏曰：「臣曩在朝，見上皇遣使冊封陛下，每遇慶節，必令群臣朝謁東廡，恩禮隆洽，群臣皆感嘆，謂上皇兄弟友愛如此。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year of Jingtai he submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject formerly at court saw the Former Emperor send envoys to invest Your Majesty; whenever festive days were met, he always ordered the ministers to attend audience at the eastern wing; grace and ritual were abundant and harmonious; all ministers sighed with feeling, saying the Former Emperor's brotherly love was like this.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year of the Jingtai reign he memorialized: "When I was at court I saw the Former Emperor send envoys to invest you as emperor. On every festive occasion he had ministers pay homage in the eastern corridor; the honor shown was warm and generous, and everyone marveled at such brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 今陛下奉天下以事上皇，願時時朝見南宮，或講明家法，或商略治道，歲時令節，俾群臣朝見，以慰上皇之心，則祖宗在天之神安，天地之心亦安矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty holds all under Heaven to serve the Former Emperor; I wish that from time to time you would attend audience at the Southern Palace, either expounding and clarifying family law, or discussing and planning the Way of governance; at seasonal festivals and appointed holidays, cause the ministers to attend audience, to console the Former Emperor's heart—then the spirits of the ancestors in Heaven will be at peace, and the heart of Heaven and Earth will also be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now you hold the realm in service of the Former Emperor. I beg you to visit the Southern Palace regularly—sometimes to discuss family propriety, sometimes to talk policy—and at each seasonal festival let ministers attend in audience to comfort the Former Emperor's heart. Then the spirits of our ancestors will rest easy, and heaven and earth themselves will be at peace.

sentences.zh: 太子者，天下之本。

translations.literal: The crown prince is the foundation of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is the foundation of the empire.

sentences.zh: 上皇之子，陛下之猶子也。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor's son is Your Majesty's nephew-like son.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Emperor's son is your own nephew in all but name.

sentences.zh: 宜令親儒臣，習書策，以待皇嗣之生，使天下臣民曉然知陛下有公天下之心，豈不美歟？

translations.literal: He ought to be ordered to be close to Confucian ministers, study books and policy documents, and wait for the birth of an imperial heir, so that ministers and people throughout all under Heaven clearly know Your Majesty has a heart of giving the realm to the public—is this not beautiful?
translations.idiomatic: Have him tutored by scholar-officials and trained in statecraft while we wait for an heir of your own—so all the realm may see that you hold the empire in trust for the dynasty. Would that not be splendid?

sentences.zh: 蓋天下者，太祖、太宗之天下。

translations.literal: For all under Heaven is the all-under-Heaven of the Grand Ancestor and the Great Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: After all, the empire belongs to the dynastic founders, Taizu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 仁宗、宣宗繼體守成者，此天下也。

translations.literal: Renzong and Xuanzong, who inherited the body and preserved the accomplishment—this is that all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong and Xuanzong received it in turn and guarded what their forebears had built—this same realm.

sentences.zh: 上皇北征，亦為此天下也。

translations.literal: The Former Emperor's northern expedition was also for this all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Emperor marched north for this very empire.

sentences.zh: 今陛下撫而有之，宜念祖宗創業之艱難，思所以系屬天下之人心，即弭災召祥之道莫過於此。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty comforts and possesses it; you ought to reflect on the hardship of the ancestors' founding enterprise and think how to bind fast the hearts of people throughout all under Heaven—there is no way surpassing this to stop calamities and summon auspicious signs."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you hold it in your care, remember how painfully the founders won it, and consider how to bind the hearts of the people to the throne—no better path exists to avert disaster and draw down blessings."

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received but went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 明年，莊以母喪，赴京關給勘合，詣東角門朝見。

translations.literal: The next year Zhuang, because of his mother's mourning, went to the metropolitan pass to receive an inspection tally and proceeded to the East Corner Gate for audience.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, while in mourning for his mother, Zhuang went to the capital checkpoint to obtain a travel pass and presented himself for audience at the East Corner Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝憶莊前疏，命廷杖八十，謫定羌驛丞。

translations.literal: The Emperor recalled Zhuang's earlier memorial and ordered him beaten eighty strokes at court, demoted to Station Master of Dingqiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor remembered Zhuang's old memorial and ordered him given eighty blows at court, then demoted to station master at Dingqiang.

sentences.zh: 天順初，召還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianshun reign he was recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 時母喪未終，復遭父喪，特予祭葬，命起復，仍官南京。

translations.literal: At that time his mother's mourning had not yet ended when he again suffered his father's mourning; he was specially granted sacrificial burial rites and ordered to resume office from mourning, still serving in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's mourning was not yet complete when his father also died; the court granted special funeral rites and ordered him back to duty in Nanjing without waiting out mourning.

sentences.zh: 天順五年就擢禮部右侍郎，改刑部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianshun he was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites and changed to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianshun he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites and then moved to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 成化初，召為刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he was summoned back as Left Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書，謚恭敏。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister; posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister and given the posthumous name Gongmin.

sentences.zh: 莊性剛，喜面折人過，而實坦懷無芥蒂。

translations.literal: Zhuang was by nature firm; he liked to rebuke people's faults face to face, yet in truth his open breast had no thorn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was stern by nature and loved to confront others' faults directly, yet he bore no grudges in his heart.

sentences.zh: 不屑細謹，好存謝賓客為歡狎。

translations.literal: He disdained minute meticulousness; he liked to keep and entertain guests for cheerful intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for petty proprieties and enjoyed keeping company with guests in easy fellowship.

sentences.zh: 既官法司，或勸稍屏謝往來，遠嫌疑。

translations.literal: Once he held office in the judicial department, some advised him slightly to shut out and decline comings and goings, keeping distant from suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered the judiciary some advised him to cut back on social visits to avoid suspicion.

sentences.zh: 莊笑曰：「昔人有言『臣門如市，臣心如水』，吾無愧吾心而已。」

translations.literal: Zhuang laughed and said: "Former people had a saying, 'My gate is like a market, my heart is like water'—I have only to be without shame before my own heart."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang laughed and said: "The ancients said, 'Though my gate be thronged like a market, my heart is clear as water'—I need only have a clear conscience."

sentences.zh: 卒之日，無以為斂，眾裒錢助其喪。

translations.literal: On the day of his death there was nothing with which to encoffin him; the multitude gathered money to assist his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he died there was not enough for his burial; colleagues pooled money to pay for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 初，景帝時，英宗在南宮，左右為離間。

translations.literal: Initially, during Emperor Jing's reign, Yingzong was in the Southern Palace, and those around him sowed discord.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, during Emperor Jing's reign, Yingzong was in the Southern Palace, and those around him sowed discord.

sentences.zh: 及懷憲太子薨，群小恐沂王復立，讒構愈甚。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Huai Xian died, petty men feared the Prince of Yi would be restored, and slanderous plotting grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Huai Xian died, petty men feared the Prince of Yi would be restored, and slanderous plotting grew ever worse.

sentences.zh: 故鐘同、章綸與莊相繼力言，皆得罪。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhong Tong, Zhang Lun, and Zhuang spoke out forcefully in succession, and all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhong Tong, Zhang Lun, and Zhuang spoke out forcefully in succession, and all were punished.

sentences.zh: 然帝頗感悟。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor was somewhat moved to reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor was somewhat moved to reflection.

sentences.zh: 六年七月辛巳，刑科給事中徐正請間言事。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the seventh month of the sixth year, Supervising Secretary Xu Zheng of the Bureau of Punishments requested a private audience to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the seventh month of the sixth year, Supervising Secretary Xu Zheng of the Bureau of Punishments requested a private audience to speak on affairs.

sentences.zh: 亟召入，乃言：「上皇臨御歲久，沂王嘗位儲副，天下臣民仰戴。

translations.literal: He was urgently summoned in and then said: "The Former Emperor ruled for many years; the Prince of Yi once held the position of heir apparent, and officials and people throughout the realm looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was urgently summoned in and then said: "The Former Emperor ruled for many years; the Prince of Yi once held the position of heir apparent, and officials and people throughout the realm looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 宜遷置所封之地，以絕人望。

translations.literal: He should be moved to the place of his original enfeoffment to cut off popular hopes.
translations.idiomatic: He should be moved to the place of his original enfeoffment to cut off popular hopes.

sentences.zh: 別選親王子育之宮中。」

translations.literal: Choose another imperial prince and rear him in the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Choose another imperial prince and rear him in the palace."

sentences.zh: 帝驚愕，大怒，立叱出之。

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and greatly enraged, and immediately shouted him out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled and greatly enraged, and immediately shouted him out.

sentences.zh: 欲正其罪，慮駭眾，乃命謫遠任，而帝怒未解。

translations.literal: He wished to punish him formally but feared alarming the multitude, and so ordered him banished to a distant post; yet the emperor's anger was not assuaged.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to punish him formally but feared alarming the multitude, and so ordered him banished to a distant post; yet the emperor's anger was not assuaged.

sentences.zh: 己，復得其淫穢事，謫戍鐵嶺衛。

translations.literal: Later, when his licentious conduct was again discovered, he was banished to garrison duty at Tieling Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his licentious conduct was again discovered, he was banished to garrison duty at Tieling Guard.

sentences.zh: 蓋帝雖怒同等所言過激，而小人之言亦未遽聽也。

translations.literal: For although the emperor was angry at the excessive words of Tong and his fellows, he did not immediately heed the words of petty men either.
translations.idiomatic: For although the emperor was angry at the excessive words of Tong and his fellows, he did not immediately heed the words of petty men either.

sentences.zh: 迨英宗復辟，于謙、王文以謀立外藩，誅死，其事遂不白雲。

translations.literal: When Yingzong restored the throne, Yu Qian and Wang Wen were executed on a charge of plotting to enthrone an outer prince; the matter was never cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong restored the throne, Yu Qian and Wang Wen were executed on a charge of plotting to enthrone an outer prince; the matter was never cleared.

sentences.zh: 倪敬，字汝敬，無錫人。

translations.literal: Ni Jing, styled Rujing, was a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Jing, courtesy name Rujing, was a native of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he passed the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the thirteenth year of the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 擢御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，畿輔饑，命出視。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign, the capital region suffered famine, and he was ordered to go out to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingtai reign, when the capital region was struck by famine, he was dispatched to investigate on behalf of the court.

sentences.zh: 請蠲田租，戶部持不可。

translations.literal: He requested exemption from land tax; the Ministry of Revenue maintained that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to waive land taxes, but the Ministry of Revenue refused.

sentences.zh: 再疏爭，竟得請。

translations.literal: He submitted another memorial pressing the point and in the end obtained approval.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a second memorial pressing the issue and ultimately won approval.

sentences.zh: 巡按山西。

translations.literal: He toured and inspected Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as touring inspector of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 時有入粟補官令，敬奏罷之。

translations.literal: At the time there was an order permitting purchase of office with grain; Jing memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was admitting grain payments in lieu of office, Jing memorialized to have the practice abolished.

sentences.zh: 戍將侵餉者，悉按治，豪猾斂跡。

translations.literal: Garrison commanders who misappropriated military pay were all investigated and punished, and the bold and unscrupulous restrained their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted every garrison commander who embezzled military pay, and the region's local bullies fell silent.

sentences.zh: 再按福建。

translations.literal: He again conducted a tour of inspection in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was next assigned to inspect Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時議將復銀冶，敬未行，抗疏論，得寢。

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed to revive silver smelting; before Jing had set out, he submitted a forthright memorial on the matter and the plan was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The court was about to reopen silver mines; Jing had not yet departed when he submitted a bold memorial against the policy, and the project was dropped.

sentences.zh: 既至，奏罷諸司器物濫取於民者。

translations.literal: After he arrived, he memorialized to abolish the practice by which various offices took goods from the people without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he memorialized to end the various offices' unauthorized exactions of goods from the populace.

sentences.zh: 鎮守內臣戴細保貪橫，敬列其罪以聞。

translations.literal: The eunuch defender Dai Xibao was greedy and overbearing; Jing listed his crimes and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: The defending eunuch Dai Xibao was corrupt and tyrannical; Jing itemized his offenses and reported them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝召細保還，命敬捕治其黨，吏民相慶。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Xibao back and ordered Jing to arrest and punish his clique; officials and commoners rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Xibao and ordered Jing to arrest his associates; officials and commoners alike celebrated.

sentences.zh: 代還，留家四月，逮治，尋復職。

translations.literal: After his successor returned, he remained at home four months, was seized and punished, and soon afterward was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour ended and he returned home, he was detained for four months and prosecuted, but was soon restored to office.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，以時多災異，偕同官吳江盛昶、江陰杜宥、蕪湖黃讓、安福羅俊、固始汪清上言：「府庫之財，不宜無故而予；

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year, because there were many calamities and anomalies at the time, together with fellow officials Sheng Chang of Wujiang, Du You of Jiangyin, Huang Rang of Wuhu, Luo Jun of Anfu, and Wang Qing of Gushi he submitted a memorial stating: "The wealth of the treasury ought not to be given away without cause;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year six, as omens and disasters multiplied, he joined his colleagues — Sheng Chang of Wujiang, Du You of Jiangyin, Huang Rang of Wuhu, Luo Jun of Anfu, and Wang Qing of Gushi — in a memorial: "Treasury funds should not be dispensed without good reason;

sentences.zh: 遊觀之事，不宜非時而行。

translations.literal: Pleasure outings ought not to be undertaken at untimely seasons.
translations.idiomatic: nor should sightseeing expeditions be mounted out of season.

sentences.zh: 曩以齋僧，屢出帑金易米，不知櫛風沐雨之邊卒，趨事急公之貧民，又何以濟之？

translations.literal: Recently, to provide vegetarian offerings for monks, treasury gold has repeatedly been taken out to purchase rice — yet how are the border soldiers who endure wind and rain, and the poor commoners who rush to serve urgent public duties, to be helped?
translations.idiomatic: Lately gold has been taken from the treasury again and again to buy rice for Buddhist offerings — yet what of the border troops battered by wind and rain, and the poor who strain to meet urgent public obligations — how are they to be sustained?

sentences.zh: 近聞造龍舟，作燕室，營繕日增，嬉遊不少，非所以養聖躬也。

translations.literal: Recently we have heard of building dragon boats, constructing banquet chambers, daily increases in construction and repair, and no small amount of play and travel — this is not how to nurture the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: We hear dragon boats are being built, pleasure chambers erected, construction growing day by day, and diversions multiplying — this is no way to safeguard Your Majesty's health.
