sentences.zh: 章綸、鐘同直言見忤，幽錮逾年，非所以昭聖德也。

translations.literal: Zhang Lun and Zhong Tong spoke bluntly and gave offense; they have been imprisoned in secret for more than a year — this is not how to display sacred virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun and Zhong Tong spoke their minds and were punished for it; they have languished in confinement for over a year — this does not reflect well on Your Majesty's virtue.

sentences.zh: 願罷桑門之供，輟宴佚之娛，止興作之役，寬直臣之囚。」

translations.literal: We wish to stop offerings to Buddhist monks, suspend the pleasures of feasting and idleness, halt construction projects, and release the imprisoned upright ministers.
translations.idiomatic: We urge you to end Buddhist offerings, abandon idle feasting, stop all new construction, and free the upright ministers now in prison."

sentences.zh: 帝得疏不懌，下之禮部。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial, was displeased, and forwarded it to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with displeasure and referred it to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 部臣稱其忠愛。

translations.literal: Officials of the ministry praised their loyalty and devotion.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry officials commended their loyal concern for the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝報聞，然意終不釋。

translations.literal: The emperor reported that he had taken note, yet his resentment was never released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor acknowledged receipt, but his anger never fully subsided.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔都御史蕭維禎考察其屬，諭令去之。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Xiao Weizhen to evaluate his subordinates and instructed that they be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the emperor ordered Censor-in-Chief Xiao Weizhen to review his subordinates and instructed that the offenders be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 御史罷黜者十六人，而敬等預焉；

translations.literal: Sixteen censors were dismissed, and among them were Jing and the others;
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen censors were removed, Jing and his colleagues among them;

sentences.zh: 皆謫為典史，敬得廣西宜山。

translations.literal: all were demoted to record clerks; Jing was sent to Yishan in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: all were relegated to county record-keeper posts; Jing was assigned to Yishan in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 英宗復辟，詔皆授知縣，乃以敬知祥符。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong restored his rule, an edict appointed them all county magistrates, and Jing was made magistrate of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, an edict restored them all as county magistrates, and Jing was appointed to Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 安遠侯柳溥器敬，西征，請以自隨，改都督府都事。

translations.literal: Marquis of Anyuan Liu Pu valued Jing; on the western expedition he requested that Jing accompany him, and Jing was transferred to Secretary in the Five Military Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Anyuan Liu Pu admired Jing; when Liu marched west on campaign, he asked that Jing accompany him, and Jing was transferred to a secretarial post in the Five Military Commissions.

sentences.zh: 逾年師還，卒。

translations.literal: A year later the army returned, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when the army returned from campaign, he died.

sentences.zh: 士類惜之。

translations.literal: Men of learning regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 盛昶等五人，皆進士。

translations.literal: Sheng Chang and the other five men were all jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Chang and the other four were all jinshi degree-holders.

sentences.zh: 昶雋爽負氣。

translations.literal: Chang was keen and forthright and possessed of fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was brilliant, forthright, and fiercely proud.

sentences.zh: 嘗按廣東，劾巡撫侍郎揭稽不職，稽坐左遷。

translations.literal: He once inspected Guangdong, impeached Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Jie Ji for dereliction of duty, and Ji was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Guangdong he impeached Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Jie Ji for neglect of duty, and Ji was demoted.

sentences.zh: 昶後為羅江知縣，擢敘州知府，並有禦寇功。

translations.literal: Chang later served as magistrate of Luojiang, was promoted to prefect of Xuzhou, and in both posts had achievements in repelling bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Chang later served as magistrate of Luojiang and was promoted to prefect of Xuzhou; in both posts he distinguished himself repelling bandits.

sentences.zh: 杜宥為英德知縣。

translations.literal: Du You was magistrate of Yingde.
translations.idiomatic: Du You served as magistrate of Yingde.

sentences.zh: 鄰境多寇，創立縣城。

translations.literal: Neighboring territories had many bandits, and he established a county seat.
translations.idiomatic: With bandits rampant in neighboring districts, he built a county seat.

sentences.zh: 嘗被圍糧盡，宥死守不下。

translations.literal: He was once besieged and grain was exhausted; You held fast and did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when the city was besieged and provisions ran out, You held firm and refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 夜縋死士焚其營，賊始驚潰。

translations.literal: At night he lowered dare-to-die soldiers to burn their camp, and only then were the bandits startled and routed.
translations.idiomatic: By night he lowered crack troops down the walls to burn the enemy camp, and the raiders panicked and fled.

sentences.zh: 移韶州通判，謝病歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Prefect of Shaozhou, then resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Prefect of Shaozhou, then retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 黃讓知安嶽，遷中府都事。

translations.literal: Huang Rang served as magistrate of Anyue and was transferred to Secretary in the Middle Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Rang served as magistrate of Anyue and was later transferred to a secretarial post in Zhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以撻錦衣衛隸，為門達所譖，戍廣西。

translations.literal: For having flogged a subordinate of the Brocade Guard, he was slandered by Men Da and was exiled to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was denounced by Men Da after flogging a Brocade Guard runner and was banished to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 赦還，復冠帶。

translations.literal: He was pardoned and returned, and his official cap and sash were restored.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he returned home and was restored to official rank.

sentences.zh: 貧甚，課耕自給。

translations.literal: He was extremely poor and supported himself by tilling assigned fields.
translations.idiomatic: Destitute, he subsisted on land allotted for cultivation.

sentences.zh: 羅俊嘗巡按四川，有廉聲。

translations.literal: Luo Jun once toured and inspected Sichuan and had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Jun had once served as touring inspector of Sichuan and earned a reputation for probity.

sentences.zh: 仕終南雄知府。

translations.literal: He served to the end as prefect of Nanxiong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Nanxiong.

sentences.zh: 楊瑄，字廷獻，豐城人。

translations.literal: Yang Xuan, styled Tingxian, was a native of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan, courtesy name Tingxian, was a native of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai he passed the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the fifth year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 剛直尚氣節。

translations.literal: Upright and blunt, he valued integrity and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and outspoken, he held fast to principle.

sentences.zh: 景帝不豫，廷臣請立東宮，帝不允。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing was unwell, court ministers requested the establishment of the Eastern Palace; the emperor did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing fell ill, court ministers petitioned to name an heir apparent, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 瑄與同官錢琎、樊英等約疏爭，會「奪門」事起，乃已。

translations.literal: Xuan together with fellow censors Qian Jin, Fan Ying, and others agreed to submit a memorial disputing this; but when the "Gate Seizure" affair arose, they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and fellow censors Qian Jin, Fan Ying, and others had planned a joint memorial on the matter, but when the "Storming-the-Gate" coup erupted, they abandoned the effort.

sentences.zh: 天順初，印馬畿內。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianshun reign, he inspected horses within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshun reign he inspected horses in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 至河間，民訴曹吉祥、石亨奪其田。

translations.literal: Reaching Hejian, the people complained that Cao Jixiang and Shi Heng had seized their lands.
translations.idiomatic: In Hejian, commoners petitioned that Cao Jixiang and Shi Heng had seized their fields.

sentences.zh: 瑄以聞，並列二人怙寵專權狀。

translations.literal: Xuan reported this and also listed the circumstances of how the two men relied on favor to monopolize power.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan reported the grievances and detailed how the two men abused imperial favor to dominate the government.

sentences.zh: 帝語大學士李賢、徐有貞曰：「真御史也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Grand Secretaries Li Xian and Xu Youzhen: "A true censor indeed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Grand Secretaries Li Xian and Xu Youzhen, "Now there is a censor in the true sense."

sentences.zh: 遂遣官按核，而命吏部識瑄名，將擢用。

translations.literal: He then dispatched officials to investigate and verify, and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to note Xuan's name for intended promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched officials to investigate, ordered the Ministry of Personnel to note Xuan's name, and intended to promote him.

sentences.zh: 吉祥聞之懼，訴於帝，請罪之。

translations.literal: Jixiang heard of this and was afraid; he complained to the emperor and asked that Xuan be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang, alarmed, appealed to the emperor and demanded that Xuan be punished.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 未幾，亨西征還，適彗星見，十三道掌道御史張鵬、盛颙、周斌、費廣、張寬、王鑒、趙文博、彭烈、張奎、李人儀、邵銅、鄭冕、陶復及御史劉泰、魏翰、康驥將劾亨、吉祥諸違法事。

translations.literal: Before long, Heng returned from the western expedition; at the same time a comet appeared. The thirteen supervising censors of the circuits — Zhang Peng, Sheng Yong, Zhou Bin, Fei Guang, Zhang Kuan, Wang Jian, Zhao Wenbo, Peng Lie, Zhang Kui, Li Renyi, Shao Tong, Zheng Mian, and Tao Fu — together with censors Liu Tai, Wei Han, and Kang Ji were about to impeach Heng, Jixiang, and others for various unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Heng returned from campaigning in the west just as a comet appeared. Thirteen circuit censors — Zhang Peng, Sheng Yong, Zhou Bin, Fei Guang, Zhang Kuan, Wang Jian, Zhao Wenbo, Peng Lie, Zhang Kui, Li Renyi, Shao Tong, Zheng Mian, and Tao Fu — together with censors Liu Tai, Wei Han, and Kang Ji were preparing to impeach Heng, Jixiang, and others for a catalogue of violations.

sentences.zh: 先一日，給事中王鉉泄於亨。

translations.literal: One day beforehand, Supervising Secretary Wang Xuan leaked the matter to Heng.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, Supervising Secretary Wang Xuan tipped Heng off.

sentences.zh: 亨與吉祥泣訴帝，誣鵬等為已誅內官張永從子，結黨排陷，欲為永報仇。

translations.literal: Heng and Jixiang wept and appealed to the emperor, slandering Peng and the others as grand nephews of the executed eunuch Zhang Yong, forming a faction to frame and entrap them, seeking revenge for Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and Jixiang went weeping to the emperor and claimed Peng and his allies were nephews of the executed eunuch Zhang Yong, banding together to frame loyal men and avenge Yong's death.

sentences.zh: 明日疏入，帝大怒，收鵬及瑄。

translations.literal: The next day the memorial arrived; the emperor was greatly angered and seized Peng and Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived the following day, the emperor flew into a rage and had Peng and Xuan arrested.

sentences.zh: 禦文華殿，悉召諸御史，擲彈章，俾自讀。

translations.literal: At the Wenhua Hall the emperor summoned all the censors, threw down the impeachment memorials, and ordered them to read them aloud themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Summoning all the censors to the Wenhua Hall, the emperor threw their impeachment drafts at them and ordered each to read his own aloud.

sentences.zh: 斌且讀且對，神色自若。

translations.literal: Bin read while also responding, his expression calm as ever.
translations.idiomatic: As Bin read his charges, he answered the emperor point by point, his composure unshaken.

sentences.zh: 至冒功濫職，帝詰之曰：「彼帥將士迎駕，朝廷論功行賞，何雲冒濫？」

translations.literal: When it came to falsely claiming merit and reckless promotion of offices, the emperor interrogated him: "They led soldiers and officials to welcome the emperor; the court assessed merit and dispensed rewards — why do you call it false and reckless?"
translations.idiomatic: On the charge of merit fraud and reckless promotion, the emperor demanded: "They led troops to welcome me home; the court rewarded them according to merit — why call that reckless?"

sentences.zh: 斌曰：「當時迎駕止數百人，光祿賜酒饌，名數具在。

translations.literal: Bin said: "At the time those who welcomed the emperor numbered only a few hundred; the Directorate of Palace Provisions bestowed wine and food, and the roster of names is fully preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Bin replied: "When the emperor was welcomed home, there were only a few hundred men — the Directorate of Palace Provisions kept a register of every name it fed and feted.

sentences.zh: 今超遷至數千人，非冒濫而何？」

translations.literal: Now promotions have been rushed to several thousand men — if this is not reckless promotion, what is?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet promotions now number in the thousands — if that is not reckless, what is?"

sentences.zh: 帝默然，竟下瑄、鵬及諸御史於獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent and in the end sent Xuan, Peng, and all the censors to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent and ultimately sent Xuan, Peng, and the other censors to prison.

sentences.zh: 榜掠備至，詰主使者，瑄等無所引，乃坐都御史耿九疇、羅綺主謀，亦下獄。

translations.literal: Flogging was applied to the utmost; they were questioned as to who had masterminded it; Xuan and the others implicated no one; then Censor-in-Chief Geng Jiuchou and Luo Qi were judged the chief plotters and also sent to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Under torture they were pressed to name their ringleader; Xuan and the others named no one. Censor-in-Chief Geng Jiuchou and Luo Qi were then declared the masterminds and imprisoned as well.

sentences.zh: 論瑄、鵬死，余遣戍。

translations.literal: Xuan and Peng were sentenced to death; the rest were sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Peng were sentenced to death; the others were banished to frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 亨等復譖諸言官。

translations.literal: Heng and the others again slandered the various remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and his allies lodged fresh accusations against the remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 帝諭吏部，給事、御史年逾三十者留之，余悉調外。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the Ministry of Personnel that supervising secretaries and censors over thirty years of age were to be kept; all others were to be transferred outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the Ministry of Personnel to retain supervising secretaries and censors over thirty and transfer the rest to provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 尚書翺列上給事中何玘等十三人，御史吳禎等二十三人。

translations.literal: Minister Ao listed and submitted Supervising Secretary He Qi and twelve others, and Censor Wu Zhen and twenty-two others.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Ao submitted a list naming Supervising Secretary He Qi and twelve colleagues, and Censor Wu Zhen and twenty-two others.

sentences.zh: 詔以玘等為州判官，禎等為知縣。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Qi and the others as prefectural vice magistrates and Zhen and the others as county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: An edict assigned He Qi and his group to posts as prefectural vice magistrates, and Wu Zhen's group as county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 會大風震雷，拔木發屋，須臾大雨雹。

translations.literal: At the same time great wind and thunder shook the earth, uprooting trees and tearing off roofs; in an instant torrential rain and hail followed.
translations.idiomatic: Then wind and thunder burst forth, uprooting trees and tearing roofs away, followed moments later by torrential rain and hail.

sentences.zh: 亨、吉祥家大木俱折，二人亦懼。

translations.literal: The great trees at the homes of Heng and Jixiang all snapped; the two men were also afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Great trees on the estates of Heng and Jixiang were snapped in two, and both men were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 掌欽天監禮部侍郎湯序本亨黨，亦言上天示警，宜恤刑獄。

translations.literal: Tang Xu, Vice Minister of Rites in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy, was originally of Heng's faction, but he too said Heaven was showing a warning and that penal cases ought to be treated with compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xu, the Vice Minister of Rites who supervised the Directorate of Astronomy and was himself a Heng ally, argued that Heaven was sending a warning and that the prisoners should be treated leniently.

sentences.zh: 於是帝感悟，戍瑄、鵬鐵嶺衛，余貶知縣，泰、翰、驥三人復職，而玘、禎等亦得無調。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor was moved to reflection; Xuan and Peng were exiled to Tieling Guard, the rest were demoted to magistrates, Tai, Han, and Ji were restored to office, and Qi, Zhen, and the others also escaped transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to repentance, the emperor sent Xuan and Peng to exile at Tieling Guard, demoted the rest to county magistrate posts, restored Tai, Han, and Ji to office, and spared He Qi, Wu Zhen, and the others from transfer.

sentences.zh: 玘、鵬行半道，適承天門災，肆赦放還。

translations.literal: Qi and Peng, halfway on their journey, encountered a disaster at the Chengtian Gate; a general pardon released them and they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi and Zhang Peng were still en route when fire destroyed the Chengtian Gate; a general amnesty brought them back.

sentences.zh: 或謂當詣亨、吉祥謝，二人卒不往，復謫戍南丹。

translations.literal: Some said they ought to go to Heng and Jixiang to offer thanks; the two men ultimately did not go and were again demoted to exile in Nandan.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged them to pay their respects to Heng and Jixiang; the two steadfastly refused and were banished again to Nandan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，並還故官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, all were restored to their former offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong came to the throne, all were restored to their former posts.

sentences.zh: 瑄尋遷浙江副使。

translations.literal: Xuan was soon transferred to Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was soon promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 按行海道，禁將校私縱戍卒。

translations.literal: He inspected the coastal routes and forbade officers and commanders from privately releasing garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Touring the coastal routes, he forbade officers from letting garrison troops go AWOL.

sentences.zh: 修捍海塘，築海鹽堤岸二千三百丈，民得奠居。

translations.literal: He repaired sea-defense embankments and built two thousand three hundred zhang of seawalls at Haiyan; the people were able to settle in security.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt sea dikes and constructed twenty-three hundred zhang of seawalls at Haiyan, allowing the people to live in peace.

sentences.zh: 為副使十餘年，政績卓然，進按察使。

translations.literal: After more than ten years as Vice Commissioner, with outstanding administrative achievements, he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a decade of distinguished service as Vice Commissioner, he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 西湖水舊可溉諸縣田四十六萬頃，時堙塞過半，瑄請浚之。

translations.literal: The waters of West Lake had formerly been able to irrigate four hundred sixty thousand qing of fields in various counties; at the time more than half was silted and blocked; Xuan requested dredging.
translations.idiomatic: West Lake once irrigated four hundred sixty thousand qing of farmland across several counties, but more than half its channels were now silted shut; Xuan petitioned for dredging.

sentences.zh: 設防置閘，以利灌溉，功未就，卒。

translations.literal: He set up defenses and installed sluice gates to benefit irrigation; the work was not completed when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He began installing flood controls and sluice gates to restore irrigation, but died before the project was finished.

sentences.zh: 海鹽人祠祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Haiyan enshrined and sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Haiyan built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 子源，字本清，幼習天文，授五官監候。

translations.literal: His son Yuan, styled Benqing, studied astronomy from youth and was appointed Director of the Five Offices of Observation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan, courtesy name Benqing, had studied astronomy since boyhood and was appointed a Director in the Five Offices of Observation.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，劉瑾等亂政，源上言：「自八月初，大角及心宿中星動搖不止。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, when Liu Jin and others misgoverned, Yuan submitted a memorial: "Since the beginning of the eighth month, the star Great Horn and the central star of Heart Constellation have shaken without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde, as Liu Jin and his faction misruled the realm, Yuan memorialized the throne: "Since the start of the eighth month, the star Great Horn and the central star of the Heart constellation have trembled unceasingly.

sentences.zh: 大角，天王之坐，心宿中星，天王正位也，俱宜安靜，今乃動搖。

translations.literal: Great Horn is the throne of the Heavenly King; the central star of Heart Constellation is the correct seat of the Heavenly King — both ought to be tranquil, yet now they are shaking.
translations.idiomatic: Great Horn is the throne of the celestial sovereign; the Heart's central star marks his rightful seat — both should rest unmoving, yet now they tremble.

sentences.zh: 其占曰：『人主不安，國有憂。』

translations.literal: The omen interpretation says: 'The ruler is unsettled; the state has worries.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication reads: 'The sovereign is ill at ease; the realm faces calamity.'

sentences.zh: 意者陛下輕舉逸遊，弋獵無度，以致然也。

translations.literal: Presumably Your Majesty's light-minded wandering and idle travel, hunting and falconry without measure, have caused this.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect this is because Your Majesty travels lightly and indulges in sport, hunting without restraint.

sentences.zh: 又北斗第二第三第四星，明不如常。

translations.literal: Moreover, the second, third, and fourth stars of the Northern Dipper shine less brightly than usual.
translations.idiomatic: The second, third, and fourth stars of the Northern Dipper also burn dimmer than they should.

sentences.zh: 第二曰天璇，后妃之象。

translations.literal: The second is called Celestial Pivot; it is the emblem of empresses and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The second star is Celestial Pivot, symbol of the empress and consorts.

sentences.zh: 后妃不得其寵則不明，廣營宮室妄鑿山陵則不明。

translations.literal: When empresses and consorts do not receive proper favor, it does not shine clearly; when palace halls are widely built and mountain tombs are recklessly excavated, it does not shine clearly.
translations.idiomatic: It dims when consorts fall from favor, when palaces are built on an extravagant scale, or when imperial tombs are recklessly opened.

sentences.zh: 第三曰天機，不愛百姓，驟興征徭則不明。

translations.literal: The third is called Celestial Secret; when the people are not cherished and levies and corvée are suddenly raised, it does not shine clearly.
translations.idiomatic: The third, Celestial Secret, dims when the people are neglected or corvée levies are suddenly increased.

sentences.zh: 第四曰天權，號令不當則不明。

translations.literal: The fourth is called Celestial Authority; when commands and edicts are improper, it does not shine clearly.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth, Celestial Authority, dims when imperial edicts go awry.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下祗畏天戒，安居深宮，絕嬉戲，禁遊畋，罷騎射，停工作，申嚴號令，毋輕出入，抑遠寵幸，裁節賜予，親元老大臣，日事講習，克修厥德，以弭災變。」

translations.literal: We humbly hope Your Majesty will revere Heaven's warning, dwell securely in the inner palace, cease playful amusements, forbid hunting excursions, stop archery on horseback, halt construction work, strictly enforce commands and edicts, do not go in and out lightly, restrain and keep distant favored consorts, cut back bestowals, draw near to senior ministers of long standing, daily engage in study and discussion, diligently cultivate virtue, and thereby quell calamities and anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray Your Majesty will heed Heaven's warning, remain securely within the palace, abandon idle diversions, forbid hunting expeditions, end mounted archery, halt all construction, enforce your decrees strictly, venture out only when necessary, keep favored consorts at a distance, curtail lavish grants, attend daily to the counsel of senior ministers, devote yourself to study, cultivate your virtue, and so avert these omens of disaster."

sentences.zh: 疏下禮部，尚書張升等稱源忠愛。

translations.literal: The memorial was forwarded to the Ministry of Rites; Minister Zhang Sheng and others praised Yuan's loyalty and devotion.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent to the Ministry of Rites, where Minister Zhang Sheng and his colleagues commended Yuan's loyal devotion to the throne.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The report was acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: An acknowledgment was returned.

sentences.zh: 迨十月，霾霧時作，源言：「此眾邪之氣，陰冒於陽，臣欺其君，小人擅權，下將叛上。」

translations.literal: By the tenth month, haze and fog occurred from time to time. Yuan said: "This is the qi of many evils; yin overwhelms yang; ministers deceive their ruler; petty men usurp power; inferiors will rebel against superiors."
translations.idiomatic: By the tenth month haze and fog appeared again and again. Yuan said: "This is the breath of accumulated corruption—yin overwhelming yang. Ministers deceive their sovereign, petty men seize power, and those below will rise against those above."

sentences.zh: 引譬甚切。

translations.literal: His analogies were very pointed.
translations.idiomatic: His analogies cut sharply to the point.

sentences.zh: 瑾怒，矯旨杖三十，釋之。

translations.literal: Jin was enraged, forged an imperial edict, had him beaten thirty strokes, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin flew into a rage, forged an imperial order, had him flogged thirty strokes, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 又上言：「自正德二年來，占得火星入太微垣帝座前，或東或西，往來不一，乞收攬政柄，思患預防。」

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial: "Since the second year of Zhengde, observations show Mars entering the Forbidden Enclosure before the Emperor's Seat, sometimes east, sometimes west, moving back and forth without fixed pattern. I beg that you gather the reins of government to yourself and guard against calamity in advance."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "Since the second year of Zhengde, Mars has been observed entering the Forbidden Enclosure before the Emperor's Seat—shifting east and west, never holding still. I beg Your Majesty to take the reins of government firmly into your own hands and guard against disaster before it comes."

sentences.zh: 蓋專指瑾也。

translations.literal: This was clearly aimed at Jin alone.
translations.idiomatic: This was plainly directed at Jin alone.

sentences.zh: 瑾大怒，召而叱之曰：「若何官，亦學為忠臣？」

translations.literal: Jin was greatly enraged, summoned him, and berated him: "What sort of official are you, that you too play at being a loyal minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin was furious. He summoned Yuan and shouted at him: "What rank are you, to play the loyal minister?"

sentences.zh: 源厲聲曰：「官大小異，忠一也。」

translations.literal: Yuan said in a loud voice: "Offices differ in rank, but loyalty is one."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan answered in a ringing voice: "Offices differ in rank, but loyalty is the same."

sentences.zh: 又矯旨杖六十，謫戍肅州。

translations.literal: Again forging an imperial edict, he had him beaten sixty strokes and banished to garrison duty at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Again Jin forged an imperial order, had him flogged sixty strokes, and banished him to frontier service at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 行至河陽驛，以創卒。

translations.literal: On the road, at Heyang post station, he died of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: En route, at Heyang post station, he died of his injuries.

sentences.zh: 其妻斬蘆荻覆之，葬驛後。

translations.literal: His wife cut reeds to cover him and buried him behind the post station.
translations.idiomatic: His wife cut reeds to shroud him and buried him behind the post station.

sentences.zh: 楊氏父子以忠諫名天下，為士論重。

translations.literal: The Yang father and son were famed throughout the realm for loyal remonstrance and were highly regarded in scholarly opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang father and son were renowned across the realm for loyal remonstrance and held in the highest esteem by scholars and officials.

sentences.zh: 而源小臣抗節，尤人所難。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan, a minor official who held fast to his integrity, was especially hard for men to emulate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuan, a lowly official who held firm to his principles, was especially difficult for others to match.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，賜謚忠懷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously granted the posthumous title Zhonghuai.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously honored with the title Zhonghuai, "Loyal and Cherished."

sentences.zh: 盛颙，字時望，無錫人。

translations.literal: Sheng Yong, styled Shiwang, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong, courtesy name Shiwang, was a native of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 周斌，字國用，昌黎人。

translations.literal: Zhou Bin, styled Guoyong, was a native of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bin, courtesy name Guoyong, was a native of Changli.

sentences.zh: 王鑒，太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 趙文博，代州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Wenbo was a native of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenbo was a native of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 彭烈，峽江人。

translations.literal: Peng Lie was a native of Xiajiang.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Lie was a native of Xiajiang.

sentences.zh: 李人儀，隆昌人。

translations.literal: Li Renyi was a native of Longchang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renyi was a native of Longchang.

sentences.zh: 邵銅，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Shao Tong was a native of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Tong was a native of Min County.

sentences.zh: 鄭冕，樂平人。

translations.literal: Zheng Mian was a native of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mian was a native of Leping.

sentences.zh: 皆進士，授御史。

translations.literal: All were jinshi graduates and were appointed censors.
translations.idiomatic: All had passed the jinshi examination and were appointed censors.

sentences.zh: 颙降束鹿知縣；

translations.literal: Yong was demoted to magistrate of Shulu;
translations.idiomatic: Yong was demoted to magistrate of Shulu;

sentences.zh: 斌，江陰；

translations.literal: Bin, Jiangyin;
translations.idiomatic: Bin, Jiangyin;

sentences.zh: 鑒，膚施；

translations.literal: Jian, Fushi;
translations.idiomatic: Jian, Fushi;

sentences.zh: 文博，淳化；

translations.literal: Wenbo, Chunhua;
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo, Chunhua;

sentences.zh: 烈，江浦；

translations.literal: Lie, Jiangpu;
translations.idiomatic: Lie, Jiangpu;

sentences.zh: 人儀，襄陽；

translations.literal: Renyi, Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: Renyi, Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 銅，博羅；

translations.literal: Tong, Boluo;
translations.idiomatic: Tong, Boluo;

sentences.zh: 冕，衡山。

translations.literal: Mian, Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 並有善政。

translations.literal: All had good administration.
translations.idiomatic: All governed their counties well.

sentences.zh: 束鹿徭役苦不均，颙為立九則法，繼者莫能易。

translations.literal: In Shulu, corvée labor suffered from gross inequity; Yong established the nine-category assessment method, which none of his successors could alter.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée duties in Shulu had long been grossly unfair; Yong instituted the nine-category assessment method, and none of his successors could improve on it.

sentences.zh: 母憂去。

translations.literal: He left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，民相率詣闕乞還。

translations.literal: When his mourning period ended, the people went in a body to the capital to petition for his return.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, the people went in a body to the capital to petition for his return.

sentences.zh: 颙再任，益不用鞭撲。

translations.literal: Yong served a second term and relied even less on the whip and the cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: On his second appointment, Yong relied even less on the whip and the cudgel.

sentences.zh: 訟者，諭之，輒叩頭不復辯。

translations.literal: When litigants came before him, once he had instructed them, they would kowtow and argue no more.
translations.idiomatic: When litigants appeared before him, a word of guidance from Yong would send them kowtowing home without another word of dispute.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑訟不決，亦皆赴訴，片言折之，各心厭去。

translations.literal: Lawsuits that neighboring counties could not settle were also brought before him; he decided them with a few words, and each party went away satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Cases that neighboring counties could not resolve were brought to him as well; he settled them with a brief ruling, and each party went away content.

sentences.zh: 郊外有隙地，爭來築室居之，遂成市，號為「清官店」。

translations.literal: Outside the city there was vacant land; people vied to build houses and settle there, until it became a market town called "Honest Magistrate's Market."
translations.idiomatic: Vacant land outside the city walls drew settlers who vied to build homes there until a market town sprang up, known as "Honest Magistrate's Market."

sentences.zh: 斌在江陰，有惠政。

translations.literal: Bin, serving in Jiangyin, had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's tenure in Jiangyin was marked by benevolent governance.

sentences.zh: 民歌曰：「旱為災，周公禱之甘露來；

translations.literal: The people sang: "When drought brings disaster, the Duke of Zhou prays and sweet dew comes;
translations.idiomatic: The people sang: "When drought brings disaster, the Duke of Zhou prays and sweet dew falls;

sentences.zh: 水為患，周公禱之陰雨散。」

translations.literal: When flood brings affliction, the Duke of Zhou prays and the rain clouds disperse."
translations.idiomatic: when flood brings affliction, the Duke of Zhou prays and the storm clouds break."

sentences.zh: 天順七年，先以薦擢開封知府。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianshun, on recommendation he was first promoted to prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianshun, on recommendation he was first promoted to prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 而颙等至憲宗嗣位，所司以治行聞。

translations.literal: When Yong and the others reached the accession of Emperor Xianzong, the relevant offices reported their record of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Yong and his colleagues reached the accession of Emperor Xianzong, the responsible offices had reported their records of good governance.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諸臣直諫為權幸所排，又能稱職，其悉予郡。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "These officials remonstrated frankly and were driven out by powerful favorites, yet they have also served competently — let them all be given prefectural posts."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "These officials spoke bluntly and were driven out by powerful favorites, yet they have also served well — let them all be given prefectural posts."

sentences.zh: 於是擢颙知邵武；

translations.literal: Accordingly Yong was promoted to prefect of Shaowu;
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Yong was promoted to prefect of Shaowu;

sentences.zh: 鑒，延安；

translations.literal: Jian, Yan'an;
translations.idiomatic: Jian, Yan'an;

sentences.zh: 文博，衛輝；

translations.literal: Wenbo, Weihui;
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo, Weihui;

sentences.zh: 烈，河南；

translations.literal: Lie, Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Lie, Henan;

sentences.zh: 人儀，荊州；

translations.literal: Renyi, Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Renyi, Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 銅，溫州；

translations.literal: Tong, Wenzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Tong, Wenzhou;

sentences.zh: 冕，衡州。

translations.literal: Mian, Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 颙復以任治劇，調延平。

translations.literal: Yong was again transferred to Yanping because he was suited to a demanding post.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was transferred again to Yanping, deemed fit for a difficult jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史上颙政績；

translations.literal: The touring investigating censor memorialized Yong's administrative achievements;
translations.idiomatic: The touring investigating censor memorialized Yong's achievements in office;

sentences.zh: 陜西、湖廣守臣亦上鑒、人儀居縣時治行。

translations.literal: Shaanxi and Huguang provincial officials also reported Jian's and Renyi's conduct while serving as county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials in Shaanxi and Huguang also reported the records of Jian and Renyi from their time as county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 皆特賜封誥。

translations.literal: All were specially granted patent letters of honor.
translations.idiomatic: All were specially granted patent letters of honor.

sentences.zh: 颙累遷陜西左布政使。

translations.literal: Yong was repeatedly promoted until he became Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yong rose through repeated promotions to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時三邊多警，歲復洊饑。

translations.literal: At the time the three frontiers had many alarms, and famine struck year after year.
translations.idiomatic: The three frontiers were under constant threat, and famine returned year after year.

sentences.zh: 颙經畫饋餉無缺，軍民悉安。

translations.literal: Yong managed supplies without shortage, and soldiers and civilians alike were secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yong managed provisions without shortfall, and both soldiers and civilians lived in security.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年召為刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Chenghua he was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Chenghua he was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of the right in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 居二年，山東旱饑，盜起，改颙左副都御史往巡撫。

translations.literal: After two years in office, Shandong suffered drought and famine, and bandits rose; Yong was changed to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent to serve as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: After two years, drought and famine struck Shandong and bandits rose; Yong was reassigned as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent to serve as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 颙至露禱，大雨霑溉，稿禾復蘇。

translations.literal: Yong arrived and prayed in the open; great rain poured down and soaked the land, and the withered grain sprang back to life.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong arrived he prayed in the open air; torrential rain poured down, and the withered grain revived.

sentences.zh: 舉救荒之政，既振，余粟尚百餘萬石。

translations.literal: He implemented famine-relief measures; once the region recovered, surplus grain still amounted to more than a million shi.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted famine-relief measures; once the region had recovered, surplus grain still exceeded a million shi.

sentences.zh: 又推行九則法於諸府，黜暴除苛，民甚德之。

translations.literal: He also extended the nine-category method to the various prefectures, dismissed the violent and removed harsh exactions; the people deeply honored him.
translations.idiomatic: He also extended the nine-category method to the prefectures, removed the violent and abolished harsh exactions, and the people deeply honored him.

sentences.zh: 居三年，以老致仕。

translations.literal: After three years he retired on grounds of age.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he retired on grounds of old age.

sentences.zh: 弘治中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Hongzhi reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 斌，歷廣東右布政使。

translations.literal: Bin served as Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Bin rose to serve as Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 初去江陰，民立生祠。

translations.literal: When he first left Jiangyin, the people erected a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he first left Jiangyin, the people erected a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 及自開封遷去，民亦涕泣追送焉。

translations.literal: When he departed Kaifeng on transfer, the people also wept and escorted him in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When he left Kaifeng on transfer, the people wept and escorted him in farewell.

sentences.zh: 鑒，初為御史，嘗於左順門面斥中官非禮。

translations.literal: Jian, when first a censor, had once at Zuoshun Gate openly rebuked eunuchs for breaches of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian first served as a censor, he once openly rebuked eunuchs at Zuoshun Gate for breaches of propriety.

sentences.zh: 中官怒甚，因考察屬都御史蕭維禎去之，維禎不可而止。

translations.literal: The eunuchs were greatly enraged and, during the performance review, tried to have Censor-in-Chief Xiao Weizhen remove him; Xiao refused and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs were furious and tried, during the performance review, to have Censor-in-Chief Xiao Weizhen remove him; Xiao refused, and the matter ended there.

sentences.zh: 文博，終巡撫河南右副都御史。

translations.literal: Wenbo ended his career as Grand Coordinator of Henan and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo ended his career as Grand Coordinator of Henan and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 烈，廣東左布政使。

translations.literal: Lie was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Lie served as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 費廣等無考。

translations.literal: Fei Guang and the others left no further record.
translations.idiomatic: No further record is given for Fei Guang and the others.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：直言敢諫之士，激於事變，奮不顧身，獲罪固其所甘心耳。

translations.literal: Commentary: Men who speak bluntly and dare remonstrate, stirred by crises, cast aside self-preservation — to suffer punishment is what they willingly accept.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Men who speak bluntly and dare remonstrate, stirred by crisis, cast self-preservation aside — to suffer punishment is what they willingly accept.

sentences.zh: 然觀尹昌隆死於呂震；

translations.literal: Yet consider Yin Changlong, who died at the hands of Lü Zhen;
translations.idiomatic: Yet consider Yin Changlong, who died at the hands of Lü Zhen;

sentences.zh: 耿通陷於高煦；

translations.literal: Geng Tong, who fell victim to Gao Xu;
translations.idiomatic: Geng Tong, who was destroyed by Gao Xu;

sentences.zh: 劉球之斃，陳鑒之系，由於王振；

translations.literal: Liu Qiu beaten to death and Chen Jian imprisoned, both because of Wang Zhen;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu beaten to death and Chen Jian imprisoned, both at the hands of Wang Zhen;

sentences.zh: 楊瑄之戍，厄於石亨、曹吉祥；

translations.literal: Yang Xuan sent to frontier garrison, beset by Shi Heng and Cao Jixiang;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan banished to frontier service, brought low by Shi Heng and Cao Jixiang;

sentences.zh: 乃至戴綸諫遊獵，陳祚請勤學，鐘同、章綸、廖莊倡復儲，倪敬等直言時事，皆用賈禍。

translations.literal: Down to Dai Lun remonstrating against hunting, Chen Zuo urging diligent study, Zhong Tong, Zhang Lun, and Liao Zhuang advocating restoration of the heir, Ni Jing and others speaking bluntly on current affairs — all brought ruin upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Dai Lun remonstrating against hunting, Chen Zuo urging diligent study, Zhong Tong, Zhang Lun, and Liao Zhuang advocating restoration of the heir, and Ni Jing and others speaking bluntly on affairs of state — all brought ruin upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 忠臣之志抑而不伸，亦可悲夫。

translations.literal: The aspirations of loyal ministers were stifled and never fulfilled — how lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: The aspirations of loyal ministers were stifled and never fulfilled — how lamentable indeed.
